**A Note from Cole, CEO of _The Flyover_** Dear Reader, Every year, auditors count how many copies America's biggest newspapers actually put in people's hands. The new numbers are brutal. Of the 25 largest papers in the country, 24 shrank last year. Average decline: 12.5%. Nearly a quarter-million daily papers, gone in a single year. _The Denver Post_ now prints about 24,000 copies a day. _The Arizona Republic_ , 33,000. _The Houston Chronicle_ , 35,000. _The Dallas Morning News_ , under 40,000. These are metros of millions. And the steepest collapse in the country belonged to _The Washington Post_ : down 21% in a single year to fewer than 88,000 print copies. The industry will tell you it's the internet. It's a convenient story, because it means none of this is their fault. Here's the story they won't tell: Americans didn't stop caring about the news. They stopped trusting the people delivering it. Somewhere along the way, the papers stopped reporting what happened and started campaigning for what they wanted to happen--and their readers noticed. Trust in the media now sits at the lowest level ever recorded. So no, that's not an audience drifting away. That's a jury coming back with a verdict. Today’s sponsor, , helps you look beyond your weight with the Body Pod, an at-home scale that tracks body composition, including estimated body fat and muscle mass. | Alaska Orders Probe of Decoy Senate Candidate Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy ordered state police Thursday to by the Democrat candidate to confuse voters in the state’s crucial Senate race, days before Tuesday’s midterm elections, and the Justice Department issued a wave of grand jury subpoenas. A New York Times investigation revealed that operatives tied to Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign and a national party committee for Alaskans named Dan Sullivan, the name of the Republican incumbent she is trying to unseat. Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher from Petersburg who has done very little campaigning, later landed on the four-way ballot. Peltola’s campaign and the committee have denied , and Peltola called the Times report a distraction. President Trump wrote on Truth Social that Peltola engaged in “election fraud” and . The Justice Department is separately suing to block certification if Sen. Sullivan narrowly loses. Economy Grows Along with Inflation The economy grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, that economists expected, led by consumer spending, according to advance estimates. Inflation kept climbing in the meantime. The Federal Reserve’s rose 0.5% in September and 3.6% from a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August, the Commerce Department announced Thursday. Core prices, which , were up 3.1% over the year. Goods prices rose 3.9% and services 3.5%, while the personal savings rate slipped to 3.8% of disposable income. The reports come the day after Federal Reserve officials at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, with two dissenting in favor of an increase to fight inflation. Star Trek’s Patrick Stewart Dies at 86 Sir Patrick Stewart, the Shakespearean actor who became Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation , at his home in Los Angeles. He was 86. His family said he had Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, calling his illness “a brief and poignant journey” and remembering him as a figure of “invincible grace.” His wife, Sunny Ozell, was at his side. But I have to tell you that nothing is guaranteed. And over the last few days, Mike Lawler and his allies have been seriously outraising us. This is going to be a really brutal fight for every single vote until the very end.

## GOP Suit Seeks Statewide Hand Count
The Potter County Republican Party [filed a federal lawsuit](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp_GdCD_4RsXLrahy7ZbIseehJGMHdkDhLdfkVe49Rwdnfn-3ee7x4T59dev4OjzLHOGoyUggjqH4sPS_A6t0RYhE5UalrPlWXJpesF7xWcfCHeYte-ie_BoRQdO_FilxpswY7c4MJLryIUAbW6jHkdhrVYimqCsssZ06C6d4IoLwaWWg_U-PozVAaSOegxMc4hIpQ60AMHHt2c6yw51CGXtkluI3o2pP0xOTE7HcQzXE9kTlpzLcVFMTu-SkDA0Jqdv_oqRoK49JAgXeR2-8j75o21I_eJz7EPZMvXhfEBtELaKdDI5ddXF94EpYTM_TPPX6jF9c-i3M-5O_g8AAP__yiGKQQ) Tuesday to block Texas from certifying the Nov. 3 election until every paper ballot statewide is counted by hand, a request now before federal Judge Matthew Kacsmaryk, a Trump appointee. Chairman Daniel Rogers and the party argue that foreign-made voting machine parts and rogue AI programs could alter results without detection. Texas already requires a partial hand-count audit when machines are used, but the suit says that isn't enough. The complaint doesn't claim that any Texas machine was ever hacked or that votes were changed. University of Houston law professor David Froomkin called the case "weak" and [expects it to be dismissed](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO8yAUBODT4A4LHtiJC4q_cZe_3dIi8ByQCFjwbCe3XyVX2HqkTzPzc1tuNqaYH__tEw291rJkPFtCIqyLK9aFZg9sjXaPmahUF94tLyBg5FJwJRbrKB64aNt5cxd-kh0aeZmUGq5yHLpglJIXFIMaRq-GUa4CnYUrgHa4CjlNXTQfTgolpBSgoZ-s9fdx0g5Bez04pgX6SKX2FJDwZdua3uXA2rvy7JIJRFtj6h-DmcF8nmfvQi35kzKYP4MYzLZSdAkZzF-BV9z2e4rO5sbbjjzY7LkreyaOCR3FkhsHGIQYJ9VvYeuq8dsZU4ptvDAtHk8b07cB_fW5w8BvAAAA___rpISw), saying the plaintiffs offer "nothing but wild conjectures."
## Silsbee Coach Saves Student
A Silsbee Middle School coach [performed the Heimlich maneuver](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkb_OnDAQxJ_GdHsya8yfgiIN3Zc2JVrWy2HF4JPtD-7ePrpTivRpZ0Yj_WZ-fc1f5IM_7j9pl7E81zgfcuUgpUiaORJvmU7JuXw7OUqJibdXPmbU2EKtweiZuPhT5oYqNy7aDXUlY90Nxti-bm21jWg1iXaLNSzDyoyLaVEsus6R4bqv_Piuq7XRda2xwdtA5JZ2aFiwcY1l1WhxvsR0K5sUeVJewyuekm4c9yqMWymPrMwPhZPC6bquW41vjCNe74TCiVLxHETh9NYVTiEyBYVT9iEvIrB754JA5i3GAB9weEhaY9ozbOL34HmDnQ75PiVBPIC3-Nsfd_g7DTxikaN4CuEFmc5_rAzBrwLlqXCyGqG3NLBeGLBFB01nNfS9bsGKYGOca43rqjS6x-VD8LntVKPvO_nwwS3_e9M54p8AAAD__yViqwI) on a choking student this week, clearing the airway and possibly saving the student's life, the district said in a Facebook post. The coach, Morgan Robberts, graduated from Silsbee High School in 2020 and is a [former All-State offensive lineman](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1ygzAQhU8jOnmkRYApVKShc9qUjJAWaycCeVgZ27fP4OQGKfdn3rzv-7qMF0eJ1uunW9CW55zHFR-csBTcRp-dj-x2ZC73gGspefPxxesIClqplazV6HyhHUfjqmAnFXpdodVdX9fNWbdNFW3nsKnPtZrrHhvQYKbOt9gqaLU69hVZ-B2U1goMnHrnwtT2xiOYYBovjMJAJW-nErHg0_GcXnnH7eTzUiUbS7mxqD8EDAKG7zksx0HAcLAIGFL2LgkYmBJPiPLNJf12hGKQDypR3pnWq4xISyIf5eJWvO-4yVtmpim9JLv9-PgzwTLRjNVmw-1BKRG3nTDqujhK71LlvzJ3Cz8BAAD__3Z-jUE). He returned to the district to teach and coach, working alongside the staff who had once coached him. "_Not all heroes wear capes_ ," the district wrote, thanking Robberts for his "quick thinking, calm demeanor, and life-saving actions." Robberts said he "was praying the whole time" and thanked God for having "his hand over the whole situation."
## Rain Soaks Texas Ahead of Halloween
Tropical Storm Vance's leftovers and Gulf moisture are spreading rain across Texas through the weekend, but forecasters from Dallas to Houston say [Halloween won't be a washout](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykULGu6yAU-xqyEQEhNBkY3pLtvvWN0SmcFCQSKjgN7d8_pb9wN8uWLdv_ftYfiCkej7-wo6X3ltcDW01IhGV1GVyocGKt9PJ4EOXiwqceqxLKcCn4IFZwFE9cNXTe3oWfZYdW3uZhGCdpxi5YPYATg9omJ6QfhR9HI_BmzKRxhElAF-0VJ8UgpBRKq34G8Hcza4dKez06pgX6SLn0FJDwDXVLn3xi6V3eu2QD0bOy4Q9TC1NLa61393rtuHSmlq-FqeWimFo8pASVNwQKWDhlDx8eIKXcEA--5YIOKl2AeMuFAifcn1iAXgUrz464mplaumL9s8WUYjU3psVjh5i-nei3X55W_Q8AAP__eBmM0A). West Texas gets the heaviest rain. Forecasters in Midland expect remnants of Vance to [stall over the region](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAUhJ8GOpB_cShc3CZdbrslOtjHsSUHI_ssJG-_Spp9gC1nRvpG-r5uyw1STtv9PzzQ0jOUZcOzZSTCurgCLjY4sDX69rgRleriq22LYGIaOBskW8BROnBR0Hu7Mj_zHi03s5T6wifdR6uCNI47pVzQMsAKAlc9G-NNuAgdpj7ZN44zyThnQolxBvDrNCuHQnmlXacY-kSljhSR8Akt5Fc5sI6uPPpsI9HeOvmvE9dOXM_zHF2sZXuv74xAEWsnrlApuYy_3RBKRQeNhg91iJBzORG3QQg1G6n1uMe9r9bvZ8o5tcl0it0fkPLnmv6q7LDiJwAA__9pvoMu) by Friday, dropping up to 6 inches in isolated spots and causing flash flooding in low-lying and urban areas. In North Texas, showers and a few thunderstorms build Friday afternoon ahead of the evening commute and linger into Saturday morning. Rain is expected to clear out from west to east by afternoon, leaving [a dry window for trick-or-treaters](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD3uozAQxU8DnZFtDAmFi23SZdst0cQzxNYaO7InEG6_Itob_Nufnt7Xn_t8hxBDev6GlSx_ljwn2mskZiqzy-B8hY1q5TdSYs7F-aOmWUs9CiVFL2dwHDaaDbRoHxIn1ZJVl6nvh6sah9ZbowbspTQTXiSBcyOhvCLSuGg5DcvYBnvaKdlLpaQ2upsA8DFOxpE2aAbXGEkYOJeOPTF9oC7xyBuVzuW1jdYzv2rT_2r0rdG3fd-7JX_MOeQUnIiAPZVG3xBihCr-A1EgJOE8JEdVFOJ3SSLlwl58Y4SHGPNOlETM-W8Va64cD4HlaIvF1x5iDHW8NEY-Vwjx24d_-uNm9b8AAAD__2A9jQk). The Houston area expects a muggy Halloween with highs in the upper 70s to upper 80s and [scattered daytime storms possible](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D3uozAUBPDTmM6Rv8ChcLEN3X_bLdHDfsSWDI7sFwi3XyXSnmDr-Wk0mj8_8w-knPbHb9jQ0Xst845ny0iEdfYFfGxwYGv0CrgTlerj1fZZCTVwKbgWM3hKB84GuuAWEUbZoZN21Lq_y6HvorMWpJWrHXu7-MWKcF-CNlZp2w96sfcuuU-dFFpIKZRRtxEgLMNoPCoTTO-ZERgSlXqjiIRvaGu-yoH15svWZReJno3pX0xNTE1f0KjUzUdoWNtHMTWtpaKHRkxNV3lV_nU8Qs7lRNz5v5w_86vxiHBcvELa-YmNeFl54rpnauqqC88z5ZzaYJkRjw1S_i6h_33wcOpvAAAA__8ydokh), though the evening looks fine for most. **A Note from Cole, CEO of _The Flyover_** Dear Reader, Every year, auditors count how many copies America’s biggest newspapers actually put in people’s hands. The new numbers are brutal. Of the 25 largest papers in the country, 24 shrank last year. Average decline: 12.5%. Nearly a quarter-million daily papers, gone in a single year. _The Denver Post_ now prints about 24,000 copies a day. _The Arizona Republic_ , 33,000. _The Houston Chronicle_ , 35,000. _The Dallas Morning News_ , under 40,000. These are metros of millions. And the steepest collapse in the country belonged to _The Washington Post_ : down 21% in a single year to fewer than 88,000 print copies. The industry will tell you it’s the internet. It’s a convenient story, because it means none of this is their fault. Here’s the story they won’t tell: Americans didn’t stop caring about the news. They stopped trusting the people delivering it. Somewhere along the way, the papers stopped reporting what happened and started campaigning for what they wanted to happen—and their readers noticed. Trust in the media now sits at the lowest level ever recorded.
So no, that’s not an audience drifting away. That’s a jury coming back with a verdict. And here’s the part the industry really doesn’t want to talk about: those readers didn’t give up on news. They went looking for someone who would just tell them the truth. Millions of them found their way to _The Flyover_ —a morning news publication built on one simple deal: We call things what they are. We keep the spin out and trust you with the facts. And _The Flyover_ stays free. It turns out that when you just give people the facts and trust them to think for themselves, people respond. So today I’m asking: will you help us continue? If news that plays it straight is something you want to see thrive, will you stand behind us? name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: More than 6,000,000 voters
body:
We’re going all in these last 4 days.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, weeks ago, the experts said Greg Abbott had this race locked up.
Today is the last day of early voting, and more than 6,000,000 Texans have already cast their ballots, and the projections based on who’s actually showing up tell a very different story:_**this race is neck and neck.**_
You made that happen. The ads, the texts, the doors our organizers knocked to bring voters to the polls — your support powered every bit of it.
For years, Abbott and his allies have tried to convince Texans that change here is impossible. **The early voting numbers are the clearest sign yet that they’re wrong.**
But we didn’t get into this race to come close. We got into it to win. And winning means bringing out even more voters: Texans who stayed home last time, and Texans who are still making up their minds. After today, there’s only one chance left to reach them: **Election Day, Tuesday, November 3rd.**
So we’re going all in. Our organizers will be knocking doors from now until polls close on Election Day, and we’re putting every dollar we have into ads and texts that reach voters before they head to the polls. Abbott can outspend us — but he can’t outwork us.
I know you haven’t given to our campaign yet. Maybe it felt like winning was out of reach — but not anymore. The early vote numbers prove it isn’t. [**Will you make your first contribution today and help us reach every last voter before polls close on Tuesday?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261030_1_ev.KkBgCp&refcode=em20261030-2586&t=2&akid=2586%2E299639%2EvEXD00)
[Donate »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261030_1_ev.KkBgCp&refcode=em20261030-2586&t=21&akid=2586%2E299639%2EvEXD00)
Thank you,
Gina
_Our records aren’t perfect – if you’ve donated with a different email address, phone number, or by check, not all of your gifts may be reflected in our accounting here. I greatly appreciate all of your support in this campaign._

subject: Speak Up: The Trump admin wants to sacrifice 23 million acres of Arctic wildlife habitat.
body:
Stop this assault on the Arctic and the irreplaceable wildlife who call it home.

Stop this assault on the Arctic and the irreplaceable wildlife who call it home.
                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6225195/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6225196/38SyG9Xl)

Act Now to Protect the Arctic (https://support.defenders.org/s/6225197/38SyG9Xl)

Defender,

Imagine half of Southern Beaufort Sea polar bears... just gone. This fragile population of polar bears has seen their population decline by nearly 50% as sea ice, essential for their survival, melts away.

Now, the Trump administration is proposing to end critical environmental reviews and fast-track oil and gas drilling across 23 million acres of public lands in Alaska's Western Arctic. This move threatens the fragile snow dens where polar bear mothers give birth and shelter their vulnerable cubs.

We only have until November 9 to make our voices heard. Click here to sign a message to Stevan Pearce, Director of the Bureau of Land Management: We will not stand by while you fast-track dangerous oil and gas development in the Western Arctic! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6225198/38SyG9Xl)

Take Action: Protect Arctic Wildlife! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6225199/38SyG9Xl)

Polar bears aren't the only species at risk. The Western Arctic is home to hundreds of thousands of caribou, snowy owls and millions of migratory birds who depend on its vast tundra and wetlands.

This proposal is another example of the administration's efforts to open the irreplaceable Western Arctic to industrial oil development — even as climate change pushes the wildlife who call it home closer to the brink of extinction.

The public comment deadline is November 9. There is little time left to make your voice heard.

Send your message now! We must stop the Trump administration and Big Oil from creating new laws at the cost of America’s wildlife and wild places. (https://support.defenders.org/s/6225200/38SyG9Xl)

Sincerely,

Christi Heun

Senior Representative, Alaska

Defenders of Wildlife

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

Defenders of Wildlife 1130 17th Street NW • Washington, DC 20036 defenders.org (https://defenders.org)

 

 
Photo Credit: Polar Bears © Susanne Miller/USFWS

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com (mailto:dpwillis67@gmail.com)

body:
Three amendments are on your Tennessee ballot, and my guest Rep. Vincent Dixie and I are voting NO on every one.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/d89bf49f70d3/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7363988?e=dc5f639d62)

| |

Hey friends,Three amendments are on your Tennessee ballot, and my guest Rep. Vincent Dixie and I are **voting NO** on every one.
[CLICK HERE to LISTEN NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/yYbXWkaeu22?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
[**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/_xpcLGHhCSd?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**
Here’s the thing: the language you’ll see in the voting booth won’t tell you the whole story. Rep. Dixie of Nashville knows the bail system inside and out. He owns a bail bonding company, and he’s upfront about that, so you’ll hear it straight from someone who’s seen it up close.We dig into Amendment 1 and what it could mean for people who are accused but not convicted, for your county jail, and for your tax bill. We break down Amendment 2, the state property tax ban, and Amendment 3, the victims’ rights amendment. And we get into why policy doesn’t belong in our state’s Constitution.Your phone has probably been blowing up with questions about these. **Send this to someone who’s voting this week.****Here’s a quick look at why we’re voting NO:**
* **Amendment 1** takes away the right to bail for people accused of 73 felonies. That could mean months in jail before trial, and your county’s taxpayers footing the bill.
* **Amendment 2** bans a state property tax Tennessee doesn’t have. It won’t change your tax bill, and it limits what future lawmakers can do.
* **Amendment 3** adds victims’ rights to the Constitution that are already in state law and may affect due process rights.

name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: For most Michiganders, this race is just getting started
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=3829%2E251025%2E01cIw5 ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=3829%2E251025%2E01cIw5 ]Abdul for US Senate

Earlier this week, I sent a note to my campaign team, the folks who’ve
poured 18 months of their lives into this. I want to share some of it with
you, because you’ve been part of this team too, whether you knocked doors,
made calls, or chipped in $10.

But first, I need to tell you this: Most Michiganders are only now tuning
in to this race. What we put in front of them in the next four days may be
the first and last thing they see of our campaign.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261030-4-ak.B7zrPC&amount=10&refcode=em20261030-3806&t=1004&akid=3829%2E251025%2E01cIw5 ]Can you donate $10 so that we can reach as many of them as
possible before polls close?

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261030-4-ak.B7zrPC&amount=10&refcode=em20261030-3806&t=1005&akid=3829%2E251025%2E01cIw5 ]Donate $10 ››

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Peter,
in just a few days, we will be waking up to an Election Day for which
we’ve been working for months, some of us more than a year and a half.

I wanted to take stock of the moment and to express my gratitude to every
one of you for all you’ve poured into this.

Millions of people are counting on us — Michiganders we have met, and
Michiganders we have yet to meet. They are counting on us to be their
voice for a fairer and kinder America.

They’re counting on us to fight for their healthcare, to take on the
corporations who’ve taken advantage of them, to fight the corruption
that’s picking their pockets. We do this for them.

God willing, we are on the cusp of changing the face of American politics.
The veneer of change — the “firsts” of this — is less what I’m talking
about than the foundations.

In America, we are supposed to have a government of the people, by the
people, and for the people. Yet we’ve watched as oligarchs, special
interests, and corporations have corrupted that ideal into something that
looks very different than what it was intended to be.

The framers intended a democracy in which we openly debate our ideas —
what we’ve got now feels more like corporations and special interests
funding both sides of an endless cycle of attack ads.

We’re challenging that system. We’re going everywhere; we’re speaking with
everyone.

It’s odd that our campaign feels new to folks when it was built on the
oldest foundations of what democracy was supposed to be in the first
place. Changing the face of American politics is simply an exercise in
civic exfoliation, clearing the gunk to take us again to the ideals of
what this was always supposed to be.

But the cusp of something is not itself accomplishing that thing.

We have a couple of days left. The vast majority of Michiganders are only
now tuning into this campaign. What feels like the end of an 18-month
journey is, for most Michiganders, the middle of an annoying month of
election season.

What we do in the next few days may be the first and last thing someone
sees of our campaign.

As exhausted, as tired, as spent as you (and I) might feel, we need to
sprint through the tape. We rest next Tuesday at 8 PM.

This work is fundamentally about other people. You cannot do politics
alone. It’s about the conversations we have together about who we are and
who we want to be.

This team is building something special. And that’s because for 18 months,
we’ve invested in, relied upon, and believed in one another. As the
pressure mounts, we need each other now more than ever.

There are no consolation prizes in politics. We win, or we don’t. That’s
it.

I’m promising you I’m going to do all I can to win. And there is no one
I’d rather be doing this with.

I’m grateful for you. I’m grateful for all you’ve poured into this. I’m
grateful for the time, the energy, the hope, the effort.

Michigan deserves our very best, now and forever.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

I’ve put everything I have into this, and I know so many of you have too.
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261030-4-ak.B7zrPC&amount=10&refcode=em20261030-3806&t=1006&akid=3829%2E251025%2E01cIw5 ]Will you chip in $10 or any amount so that every Michigander just
tuning in hears from us before they vote?

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261030-4-ak.B7zrPC&amount=10&refcode=em20261030-3806&t=1025&akid=3829%2E251025%2E01cIw5 ]Donate $10 ››

Yours in the work,

Abdul

[ ]Donate $10 ›› Peter, in just a few days, we will be waking up to an Election Day for which we’ve been working for months, some of us more than a year and a half. I wanted to take stock of the moment and to express my gratitude to every one of you for all you’ve poured into this. Millions of people are counting on us — Michiganders we have met, and Michiganders we have yet to meet. They are counting on us to be their voice for a fairer and kinder America. They’re counting on us to fight for their healthcare, to take on the corporations who’ve taken advantage of them, to fight the corruption that’s picking their pockets. We do this for them. God willing, we are on the cusp of changing the face of American politics. The veneer of change — the “firsts” of this — is less what I’m talking about than the foundations. In America, we are supposed to have a government of the people, by the people, and for the people. Yet we’ve watched as oligarchs, special interests, and corporations have corrupted that ideal into something that looks very different than what it was intended to be. The framers intended a democracy in which we openly debate our ideas — what we’ve got now feels more like corporations and special interests funding both sides of an endless cycle of attack ads. We’re challenging that system. We’re going everywhere; we’re speaking with everyone. It’s odd that our campaign feels new to folks when it was built on the oldest foundations of what democracy was supposed to be in the first place. Changing the face of American politics is simply an exercise in civic exfoliation, clearing the gunk to take us again to the ideals of what this was always supposed to be. But the cusp of something is not itself accomplishing that thing. We have a couple of days left. The vast majority of Michiganders are only now tuning into this campaign. What feels like the end of an 18-month journey is, for most Michiganders, the middle of an annoying month of election season. What we do in the next few days may be the first and last thing someone sees of our campaign. As exhausted, as tired, as spent as you (and I) might feel, we need to sprint through the tape. We rest next Tuesday at 8 PM. This work is fundamentally about other people. You cannot do politics alone. It’s about the conversations we have together about who we are and who we want to be. This team is building something special. And that’s because for 18 months, we’ve invested in, relied upon, and believed in one another. As the pressure mounts, we need each other now more than ever. There are no consolation prizes in politics. We win, or we don’t. That’s it. I’m promising you I’m going to do all I can to win. And there is no one I’d rather be doing this with. I’m grateful for you. I’m grateful for all you’ve poured into this. I’m grateful for the time, the energy, the hope, the effort. Michigan deserves our very best, now and forever. I’ve put everything I have into this, and I know so many of you have too. [ ]Will you chip in $10 or any amount so that every Michigander just tuning in hears from us before they vote? [ ]Donate $10 ›› Yours in the work, Abdul [ Abdul ]Abdul El-Sayed

He is staring down a cataclysmic loss on Tuesday. Democrats are now favored to win back the Senate, and it has him completely unraveling.
One of the states paving the path for Dems to retake the Senate is none other than Alaska, where Dem Mary Peltola has been leading in recent polls against MAGA's Dan Sullivan.
So naturally, the President of the United States is now demanding that Alaska's Senate election be canceled, all because another man named Daniel J. Sullivan is on the ballot:

Peter —
In this moment of blatant tyranny and widening inequality, it is my deep conviction that our country needs James Talarico — a true fighter for the people — in the U.S. Senate.

I’ve spent my career as a student of history.
I’ve learned that democracy is a fragile, imperfect project — one that requires constant effort and vigilant defense. As powerful interests take their aim at the strongholds of our institutions, that vigilance has never been more important.

Decades of this pay-to-play politics have put them ahead — and left the rest of us behind.

The special interests at the top know James Talarico will put people before their profits. So they are spending massive sums of money to tear him down, divide Texans, and preserve the system that lines their pockets. # **▶️: Two Candidates. Two Very Different Visions.**
The polls are open, and Election Day is just four days away. But how much do you really know about my opponent?[**_If you're not familiar with who she is or what she stands for, watch my video below._**](https://1xz3r.mjt.lu/lnk/EAAACatlAi4AAc7mEYwAA-Neh6MAAYKKXNoAoUWGADIMFwBq5IcQ8QaerOkHSjK8H10va87zQgAtq28/2/O2OTva0_-CqO2PJQ0aCW9g/aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL21lLXZzLWhlcg)
| [](https://1xz3r.mjt.lu/lnk/EAAACatlAi4AAc7mEYwAA-Neh6MAAYKKXNoAoUWGADIMFwBq5IcQ8QaerOkHSjK8H10va87zQgAtq28/3/Jma6h7oMFSLaSINQqwiuOA/aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL21lLXZzLWhlcg)
---
My opponent, Jessica Hart Steinmann, embraces the **America First****** message, emphasizing conservative values, strength, and national pride. My approach is******Community First****,** focusing on the everyday concerns of the people who live and work in District 8.[__As my recent blog pointed out, we have quite a bit in common.__](https://1xz3r.mjt.lu/lnk/EAAACatlAi4AAc7mEYwAA-Neh6MAAYKKXNoAoUWGADIMFwBq5IcQ8QaerOkHSjK8H10va87zQgAtq28/4/AVva5HTiYExef_CMMYv-wA/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubGF1cmE0dHguY29tL3Bvc3Qvc2ltaWxhcml0aWVzLWFuZC1kaWZmZXJlbmNlcw) We're both women, mothers, and members of the same generation. But our political priorities are where the differences emerge.My campaign has focused on rising prices, affordable healthcare, public education, and the everyday challenges facing working families. After the Ball: How America Will Conquer Its Fear and Hatred of Gays in the 90's (Doubleday) opens with the sentence no movement strategist is supposed to write: "The gay revolution has failed." From there, Marshall Kirk, a neuropsychiatry researcher, and Hunter Madsen, a public-relations consultant, diagnose why -- parades and slogans had failed -- and prescribe what would win instead: advertising. Kirk was dead by 1990, cause never publicly disclosed. The book he left behind ran the country for the next thirty-six years.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/806107ee-3f95-46cd-988f-abb79605336e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This was not a manifesto of grievance; it was a marketing plan. It grew out of a February 1988 war conference of 175 activists at Warrenton, Virginia, and out of a November 1987 article the pair published in Seattle's Guide magazine under the pen name Erastes Pill -- "The Overhauling of Straight America." Its stages had the romance of a spreadsheet: Desensitize. Jam. Convert...

| | Hello my Friend, As we mark 250 years since the Declaration of Independence, it’s worth asking: **_[What did 1776 really mean—and why does it still matter today?](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckc2K2zAUhZ9G3tnox5bshRdDnbSzyJQ2A0NXRtW9cS7IkrDktI9fDJMX6Pa7l-_AOR-X-WLJU1je7Ioj5TxDhBn_Jh83LHe8xT0AhSVtFBylWXKpa8FrxWfrCj1wbm0FYydFf-srHIUZlNKiF311HxWqDnmnWjXg4PStA2cAOo1db21rflc0Hj7BFReSK84b1NBZY90A2jkDnLV8T2ALNhQyAWYXY0rRUyGXm7gtlR_vpaTM1AuTZybPFG6xuZP3GazHBmFn8iyM0bVztn4QYKwzboSZqXPGZcVQvkRApibOBZdvXLby9eswfZ9OpyuTei_rnOO-ueMlbTEndIXC8nlaEWhfmZpwteQ_obNrsrQEpqYj-kljKBgKU9PHt1-Xl_f308_5h6lfr9f6WUO1jZD-kPeUtWEtXw5p4-Jalf8d5zHKfwEAAP__e4aeog)_** Hillsdale College has created a FREE video lecture series titled **“1776”** that explores these and other questions. It takes a thoughtful look at the ideas, events, and debates surrounding the Declaration of Independence and the American Revolution. **You can receive instant access to this free video series about 1776 today using this secure link:** [https://info.hillsdale.edu/1776-cca-video-series](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckc2K2zAUhZ9G3tnox5bshRdDnbSzyJQ2A0NXRtW9cS7IkrDktI9fDJMX6Pa7l-_AOR-X-WLJU1je7Ioj5TxDhBn_Jh83LHe8xT0AhSVtFBylWXKpa8FrxWfrCj1wbm0FYydFf-srHIUZlNKiF311HxWqDnmnWjXg4PStA2cAOo1db21rflc0Hj7BFReSK84b1NBZY90A2jkDnLV8T2ALNhQyAWYXY0rRUyGXm7gtlR_vpaTM1AuTZybPFG6xuZP3GazHBmFn8iyM0bVztn4QYKwzboSZqXPGZcVQvkRApibOBZdvXLby9eswfZ9OpyuTei_rnOO-ueMlbTEndIXC8nlaEWhfmZpwteQ_obNrsrQEpqYj-kljKBgKU9PHt1-Xl_f308_5h6lfr9f6WUO1jZD-kPeUtWEtXw5p4-Jalf8d5zHKfwEAAP__e4aeog) In six engaging lectures, scholars walk through the principles and turning points that shaped our nation’s founding—along with the military, economic, and moral dimensions of the Revolution. **These are the topics you’ll explore:**
* The story of the Declaration of Independence
* Lexington and Concord
* The economics of the Revolution
* Keys to American victory
* Sermons of the Revolutionary era

It's easy to win an argument when everyone in the room already agrees with you.
But we cannot keep talking exclusively to one another and expect the rest of the country to understand what we believe--or why.
_**[I 've decided to step into the arena.](https://substack.com/redirect/5bfe0cf1-eb1c-4ce6-9116-8fb187680759?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/5bfe0cf1-eb1c-4ce6-9116-8fb187680759?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_To enter spaces outside our bubble. To explain our positions, defend our principles, answer difficult questions, and challenge assumptions about who we are.
Today, that work takes me to **BBC World Service 's Newshour at Midtown Scholar Bookstore in Harrisburg**, for a conversation focused on Pennsylvania's midterm elections and what our commonwealth may reveal about the direction of the nation.
**Come out, listen, and show your support.**
And I'm also asking you to help me keep doing it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/87854aa7-1ba1-4c5f-8e45-7c8bbbadaf28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

If a paid subscription isn't possible right now, come out today. Share this invitation. Forward my work to someone who might never otherwise hear this perspective.
You don't have to agree with every word I say to believe that our positions deserve a thoughtful, forthright voice in the conversation.
**I 'm willing to step into the arena. I hope you'll stand with me.**

name: Enoch for Congress
subject: The last blue wave skipped Ohio. Not this time.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Vanessa Enoch for Congress
body:
A nickel a message, and 4 days to go

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/6d1NPxI6uuJ?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
| | | | | | Hello Peter,

I want to start with a simple thank you.
When I asked for help with our digital ads and text campaigns, you stepped up.
Because of you, our message is reaching voters across Ohio’s 8th District who too often get overlooked. That matters, and I don’t take it for granted.
But here’s what keeps me up at night: **the last time there was a blue wave in this country, it skipped Ohio.** We cannot let that happen again. We can’t get complacent, and we can’t take our foot off the gas. Not now, with Election Day just four days away.
**Here’s where we stand, and where you can make the biggest difference:**
**1\. Help us send 103,000 more text messages.**
We still need to reach rural and apartment voters, two communities that traditional campaigns often miss. Reaching all of them costs just **$5,166**. That’s about **five cents a message** , the most affordable way to put our message directly in voters’ hands. Every gift, of any size, gets us closer.

---
| [Chip in now](https://us.list-manage.com/BWKgTlzftUY?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
---
| |

**2\. Drop literature in your community.**
We need volunteers to drop lit in about 10 communities across Butler and Hamilton Counties this weekend. A few hours of your time can put our message on hundreds of doorsteps.
**3\. Place signs at polling places on Monday night.**
The night before the election, we need help placing signs at polling places across Hamilton County, so ours is one of the first names voters see when they arrive Tuesday morning. If you can give an hour or two on Monday evening, we’d love your help.

**4\. Call voters and remind them to vote.**
We need phone bankers to call voters and remind them to get to the polls. A friendly reminder from a real person can be the difference between someone meaning to vote and actually voting. You can make calls from home and from anywhere in the US, on your own schedule, and we’ll give you everything you need to get started.
---
| [Volunteer](https://us.list-manage.com/7Wx9Y7sA8eq?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
---
| |

**5\. Celebrate with us on Election Night.**
After all the hard work, I want us together when the results come in. Please make a plan to join our Election Night Watch Party. RSVP below.
**Election Night Watch Party Details**
Tuesday, November 3, 2026 · 7:00 PMThe Pike 2 Bar & Grill10010 Springfield Pike, Cincinnati, OH 45215

Don't go to sleep on election night wishing you did more. That's the standard our Turning Point Action team is holding itself to. Right now, they're all gas, no brakes, and I couldn't be more proud of them. Everything this team is doing is more than just showing up right before November, because that's not what actually wins elections. It's about building real connections while reaching voters where they are, in their neighborhoods.

It takes years of preparation, with our door-knockers building relationships and earning trust. This is what my husband built Turning Point Action to do. Charlie wanted voting to become a habit for every America-loving patriot in this country, and our team is making that dream a reality, one front door at a time. Here's a look at what our team is doing on the ground right now: ✅ Hosting over 500 Super Chase events nationwide up until Election Day, activating people to chase votes in their own communities. ✅ We have trained and deployed 850+ full-time ballot chasers across key states, and the number is increasing by the day. ✅ Making sure voters in key states have a plan to submit their vote, through the work of our Chase the Vote team. ✅ Working day and night at headquarters so our field teams have everything they need to identify and reach every possible voter. ✅ Calling, texting, and writing postcards to voters, and hosting community events to get out the vote. ✅ Developing the "Freedom Ticket" as a personalized voter guide for patriots to use at the voting booth in key battlegrounds. ✅ Building permanent infrastructure in the new "Red Wall" states of Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire. When I see this machine at work, I see Charlie's vision growing stronger across America.

name: Katie Hobbs
subject: The polls said I’d lose
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
#

Peter, I want to tell you about the last week of the 2022 election.
**The final RealClearPolitics polling average had Kari Lake beating me by 3.5 points.** Nine of the last ten polls in the RCP average had me tied or behind. One of them, from a Democratic pollster, had me down 4.
Then the votes were counted. **I won by 17,117 votes, less than one percentage point.**
The polls this year look better, and I’m grateful for that. But our 2022 race taught me that a lead in the polls and a win on Election Day are two very different things. And when you look closely, the latest polls all show this race within the margin of error:
• Emerson Emerson College’s latest poll of the race: Hobbs 44%, Biggs 43%
• NextGen Polling: Hobbs 39%, Biggs 37.5%, with more than 1 in 5 voters still undecided
• The Tarrance Group: Hobbs 52%, Biggs 48%

In 2022, the polling average missed by more than 4 points. **A miss like that this year would erase every one of those leads.**
That’s a coin flip. And Arizonans have been voting since October 7th.
Andy Biggs just needs the polls to be a little wrong, the way they were in 2022, and he wins. He wants people like us to assume we’re leading and get comfortable.
I’m not going to do that. I’m running this final stretch like I’m 3.5 points behind, and I’m asking you to join me with that same urgency, for just a few more weeks.

clean_body: Peter, I want to tell you about the last week of the 2022 election. The final RealClearPolitics polling average had Kari Lake beating me by 3.5 points. Nine of the last ten polls in the RCP average had me tied or behind. One of them, from a Democratic pollster, had me down 4. Then the votes were counted. I won by 17,117 votes, less than one percentage point. The polls this year look better, and I’m grateful for that. But our 2022 race taught me that a lead in the polls and a win on Election Day are two very different things. And when you look closely, the latest polls all show this race within the margin of error: • Emerson Emerson College’s latest poll of the race: Hobbs 44%, Biggs 43% • NextGen Polling: Hobbs 39%, Biggs 37.5%, with more than 1 in 5 voters still undecided • The Tarrance Group: Hobbs 52%, Biggs 48% In 2022, the polling average missed by more than 4 points. A miss like that this year would erase every one of those leads. That’s a coin flip. And Arizonans have been voting since October 7th. Andy Biggs just needs the polls to be a little wrong, the way they were in 2022, and he wins. He wants people like us to assume we’re leading and get comfortable. I’m not going to do that. I’m running this final stretch like I’m 3.5 points behind, and I’m asking you to join me with that same urgency, for just a few more weeks. We have a historic opportunity to put a stop to this runaway authoritarianism
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2564%2E791427%2E9EbzT5)
Friend, the stakes of the election on Tuesday can not be overstated.
Minnesota knows them well.
We watched as Trump sent ICE into our streets to harass our neighbors, racially profile people of color, break into homes, abuse protesters, detain thousands, and kill two of my constituents with impunity.
**We responded by mobilizing sweeping resistance to the federal takeover.**
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-oct26.dpq_H3&refcode=em261030-1-subs&t=2&akid=2564%2E791427%2E9EbzT5)

Neighbors organized group chats and meet-ups. Friends educated each other about their rights. Parents protected each other's kids. Legal observers exposed ICE’s abuse. Workers went on strike and took to the streets. Communities pulled together resources for mutual aid.

What happened in Minnesota this year was a revolutionary act of solidarity in defense of civil rights. The election on Tuesday is our chance to push this movement even further and take the power to hold ICE accountable into our own hands.
If we elect a progressive majority, we can end Congress’s rubber stamp on the Trump agenda, investigate and root out ICE’s crime and corruption, and put forward real proposals to abolish ICE.
So please, with just days to go, every dollar you can give helps us stay organized and turn out the vote on Tuesday:

clean_body: No corporate PAC checks, just folks like you chipping in $10. | | | = Friend — I'm reaching out to ask for $10. I’m sorry to be so direct, but we’re approaching one of the most important deadlines of the race. Our very last end-of-month deadline is TOMORROW, and we need your help to get us back on track toward our $3 million grassroots goal. = | | = There are two ways this could go: If we fall short of our $3 million goal, Sen. Marshall’s corporate PAC allies will be emboldened to spend even more to dominate the airwaves in these final days. But if we reach, or even exceed, our goal, we’ll prove that no amount of shady money can stop our momentum. I know $3 million is ambitious. But we’re doing things differently: We’re raising $3 million dollars from thousands of grassroots donations from folks just like you. Trust me, this isn’t the easy route. = But once we get there, we will not only have the funds to fight back against massive spending by Sen. Marshall and his allies, but we will also show the country what we’re made of: thousands of grassroots supporters who believe that, together, we can build a better Kansas and a more honest, decent government for everyone. The tides are turning. Experts have called our race a toss-up — meaning we really can win. That’s why we’re pushing so hard in these final days to fight back against the millions spent against us. = If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | = I’m so moved by your commitment to our cause. In gratitude, Adam | Adam Hamilton is a husband, father, pastor and fifth-generation Kansan. Now, he’s running for U.S. Senate as an independent-minded Democrat. Just like you, he’s tired of the chaos and corruption in Washington that is harming our farmers, raising costs at the checkout line and making critical health care services unattainable. He hears your concerns and is ready to get to work for you. Recent polling shows Adam neck-and-neck in this race, and with your help, we can win big this November. = | | = | | = | This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com Rather donate by check or by mail? body:
Eugene won’t denounce it and now the Green New Deal’s biggest fan is coming to VA-07.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/NSG0dQw32mR?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Friends and Neighbors,
Yevgeny “Eugene” Vindman fled the Soviet Union as a kid.
But Yevgeny just announced he’s bringing _**Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez,**_ the face of the modern American socialist movement for a GOTV rally in Prince William County.
_**Think about that for a second.**_
In a district full of military families, small-business owners, and people who just want their electric bills and grocery prices to stop climbing, the best Yevgeny can do is fly in the congresswoman who once said the world would end in 12 years if we didn’t ban fossil fuels, championed the Green New “Scam,” and treats the border like a suggestion.
_**This is Yevgeny’s cry for help.**_
While Yevgeny is busy importing national progressive celebrities and dodging basic questions about not denouncing socialism, running this campaign the old fashion way: talking to actual voters across the district about energy, affordability, border security, and results.
_**He can have AOC. We’ll take the district.**_
Election Day is November 3. Every dollar we raise this week goes straight into the ground game that counters the circus coming to town Friday night.

Let’s send Yevgeny packing.
[**Chip in $25, $50, or $100 if you can.**](https://us.list-manage.com/Vygs_Y6OBu2?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)

One team. One fight.
****

**Republican Nominee for U.S. Congress****Virginia’s 7th Congressional District**

disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY FRIENDS OF SHERROD BROWN
body:
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142502521/657161083/-1024831887?refcode=email_fr_gmailnd_jtk6547&refcode2=0de7d79b-64d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZGU3ZDc5Yi02NGQ0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nPW7jHqWOhs_hZjnqYyEUEi3zg3SboLoakOJVo2ekiY=)
---
Hi, I didn’t decide to run for U.S. Senate because it’d be easy. After all, I lost my last race, and the GOP had spent a record amount attacking me.

Now we’re really being put to the test: **President Trump has come to Ohio three times.** This is once again one of the most expensive races in the country, and polls show it’s neck and neck.

Plus: At the eleventh hour, the top GOP super PAC in charge of holding the Senate majority announced the launch of another seven-figure ad buy full of lies statewide.

That’s because Senate control hinges on this battleground race – and with just four days left to go, National Republicans and their corporate special interest backers are terrified.

**So if you’re ready to flip this seat, I’d really appreciate you chipping in what you can today to help my campaign keep up this momentum across the finish line.**

You can use this link to donate: [**_https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sherrod-email-q4-2026_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142502522/657161084/-1024831887?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=email_fr_gmailnd_jtk6547&refcode2=0de7d79b-64d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZGU3ZDc5Yi02NGQ0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nPW7jHqWOhs_hZjnqYyEUEi3zg3SboLoakOJVo2ekiY=)

I thought I was finished with elected office after 2024. But then I watched what Jon Husted was doing with his time in the Senate. Everything we fought for, from workers’ rights to health care, got pushed aside for tax breaks for the wealthy and data centers driving up costs.

I knew I could help. I knew I could make a difference for working Ohioans. So I came off the sidelines. I’m so glad I did. And I’m even more glad you’re with me.

Hey everyone, Matt here.
The Overton window has shifted, and I really need to talk about it again.
In my last article about political ethics, I wrote about Vivek Ramaswamy's ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged biological mother. The ad itself was disturbing. But watching people defend it as good politics or an acceptable campaign tactic showed how much our standards have changed.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/480629bf-02ae-4666-baa9-dbd6a3d17e38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [How Low Will We Go: The Death of Political Decency in America](https://substack.com/redirect/480629bf-02ae-4666-baa9-dbd6a3d17e38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat)| | *
---|---|---
| Oct 21
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/480629bf-02ae-4666-baa9-dbd6a3d17e38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We have shifted in our intellectual and moral honesty. Democrats are quick to call Republicans unethical, and Republicans do the same to Democrats. Yet when we talk about campaign tactics, we increasingly skip the question of whether something is right or wrong.
Instead, we ask: Did the other guy do it? Can we use it as a political talking point? If they did it, does that mean we can do it, too?
Somewhere in that conversation, we stopped asking whether we should.
The controversy surrounding Mary Peltola's Senate campaign in Alaska is another example. And Democrats should be willing to call it out.
* * *
## Two Dan Sullivans on the Ballot
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d0a05155-cb67-4dbb-89de-dfc713049e91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Mary Peltola is a former Alaska congresswoman who lost her reelection campaign in 2024 and is now running for the U.S. Senate against Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan.
[The New York Times reported ](https://substack.com/redirect/7b1d5b53-c07e-4cb6-afb9-76658ed31335?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)that senior members of her campaign worked with Democratic operatives and personnel from the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, or DSCC, on a project to shape the ballot in her favor.
Part of that effort involved searching Alaska voter records for people named Dan Sullivan. Another Dan Sullivan, a retired teacher from Petersburg, ultimately entered the race and appeared on the general-election ballot alongside the incumbent.
The apparent strategy was to confuse at least some voters into selecting the wrong Sullivan.
The investigation described internal communications, recruitment efforts, and discussions involving campaign aides and DSCC personnel. Peltola's former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, said Peltola was "definitely aware," although she was not directly organizing the operation. Rios later tried to retract her statements, and the newspaper proceeded with its reporting.
Peltola denies knowing about the effort, and the DSCC denies involvement in recruiting the candidates. Those denials sit alongside the communications and accounts described in the investigation.
There is also money to account for. The pro-Peltola 49th State PAC reportedly paid approximately $87,000 to Wingspan Strategies, a consulting firm co-owned by an operative identified in the recruitment effort. The amount spent specifically on recruitment remains unresolved.
This was an organized effort to gain an electoral advantage by changing who appeared on the ballot. In the case of the second Sullivan, the shared name was the point.
* * *
## "Just Read the Ballot" Is Not a Defense
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ab028b39-d844-437d-92f6-55530d7531ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The response from some Democrats has been that the ballot clearly distinguishes the candidates. Read it carefully, they say, and you can tell which Sullivan is which.
That does not change the practice.
Somebody commenting on my Facebook post treated it as something funny, a **way to watch Republicans lose their minds**. But deliberately trying to confuse people while they vote is not a joke.
Let's say 99% of voters understand exactly what is happening. What about the other 1%?
The strategy does not require everybody to vote for the wrong candidate. It depends on enough people being distracted, rushing, or simply not paying close attention when they find the name they intended to select.
Alaska is a Republican-leaning state. For a Democrat challenging a Republican incumbent, small margins matter. One vote, two votes, a hundred votes. Campaigns fight over those numbers because they can change an election.
You can point to the middle initials, party labels, and other distinctions on the ballot all day. The ethical question remains: Why organize a search for somebody with your opponent's name in the first place?
I think deliberately engineering that kind of confusion should be illegal. We should certainly be able to agree that it is unacceptable without waiting for a court to tell us what our standards are.
* * *
## The Same Dirty Tricks in Ohio's 7th
In Ohio's 7th District, Congressman Max Miller has been attacking Brian Poindexter with claims about an extensive police record, including crack cocaine allegations and swallowing crack during a traffic stop.
But those drug allegations involved a different Brian Poindexter. The two men were born in the same year, but in different months. **The other Brian Poindexter is also Black.**
Miller put another man's record in front of voters as though it belonged to his opponent. That is a sleazy, deceptive tactic that depends on people accepting the accusation without noticing that the records belong to somebody else.
Democrats are right to call that out. But those same Democrats should be willing to condemn the Alaska ballot scheme. You cannot be outraged when a Republican uses a shared name to mislead voters and then laugh it off as clever politics when Democratic operatives exploit a shared name to confuse them.
The standard has to apply even when your own party benefits.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d41d093d-5ff7-4c7d-94c3-fc928d06d41d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
## Everybody Has an Excuse for Their Own Side
Republicans are furious about the Alaska story. Yet some of those same Republicans defended Ramaswamy's decision to use Acton's estranged mother against her, despite the documented history of childhood abuse and her mother remaining with the accused abuser.
Now some Democrats are defending the Alaska tactic with essentially the same argument: Get over it. We need to win.
That is exactly what I am talking about.
The objection disappears when the tactic becomes useful to our side. Suddenly, people who were demanding decency last week are explaining why decency is a luxury we cannot afford this week. Armchair moral justice warriors.
And there is always another example ready. Republicans did something similar somewhere else. Democrats have done worse. Somebody got away with it in the last election. The whataboutism that takes over the debate.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/cc2b9c6a-577b-44b4-b8cd-9e547166049b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [When Debate Dies, Democracy Weakens](https://substack.com/redirect/cc2b9c6a-577b-44b4-b8cd-9e547166049b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat) and [Dani Pajak](https://substack.com/profile/261941492-dani-pajak)| | *
---|---|---
| Jul 17
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/cc2b9c6a-577b-44b4-b8cd-9e547166049b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
How does any of that answer whether we should be doing it now?
If every unethical act becomes permission for the other party to do the same thing, the standard can only keep getting worse. Each campaign inherits the last campaign's worst behavior and treats it as the new starting point.
Then we act surprised when somebody pushes it further.
* * *
## We Cannot Keep Moving the Line
We have to do better.
The Overton window cannot keep shifting until there are no rules, no standards, and no norms we are willing to uphold. Those things are part of what allows this country to function.
The United States cannot run indefinitely on the idea that whatever helps your party win is acceptable.
The tactics described in the reporting about Peltola's campaign and Senate Democratic personnel deserve to be called out. So does Miller's use of another Brian Poindexter's record. So does Ramaswamy's exploitation of Acton's childhood trauma.
Our willingness to condemn bad campaigning cannot depend on which candidate benefits.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/578115f7-31d8-4ba7-af9a-1b551e4a430f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Fabricated Wedgewood Polls In Ohio Election Coverage](https://substack.com/redirect/578115f7-31d8-4ba7-af9a-1b551e4a430f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat)| | *
---|---|---
| Oct 22
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/578115f7-31d8-4ba7-af9a-1b551e4a430f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
If we want people to trust elections, we cannot excuse attempts to confuse them when they vote. If we want campaigns to tell the truth, we cannot defend misleading attacks because we dislike the person being targeted. And if we want basic decency in politics, we have to demand it from the candidates we support.
Somebody has to say that a tactic is unacceptable before it becomes another precedent everyone points to next time.
Because the window is moving so drastically and so quickly that we can barely keep up. Every time we excuse it, we help move it again.
I'll see you closer to election night to talk about where these races stand.

name: Gabe Amo
subject: 🚨 Red Alert 🚨4 DAYS LEFT
body:

| | Peter, Indigenous Americans weren't recognized as U.S. citizens until 1924. Some states kept Native people from the ballot box for decades more — New Mexico didn't allow them to vote until 1948. That's within living memory. **Elders in Pueblo communities today were alive when their parents couldn't legally cast a ballot in their own homeland.** Now hold that history up against what's on the ballot in 18 days: **Mary Peltola** , fighting to flip the Senate seat the majority runs through. **Peggy Flanagan** , one race from becoming the first Native American woman ever to serve in the Senate. **Deb Haaland** , running to govern the very state that barred her people from voting until 1948 — as the first Native American woman elected governor anywhere. **Sharice Davids** and **Claire Valdez** , fighting for the House seats a Democratic majority needs. Five Indigenous women. The Senate, the House, and a governorship. And with your support, we will help all five of them win. clean_body: There are elders alive today who remember when this was impossible There are elders alive today who remember when this was impossible | ~~ | | Peter, Indigenous Americans weren't recognized as U.S. citizens until 1924. Some states kept Native people from the ballot box for decades more — New Mexico didn't allow them to vote until 1948. That's within living memory. Elders in Pueblo communities today were alive when their parents couldn't legally cast a ballot in their own homeland. Now hold that history up against what's on the ballot in 18 days: Mary Peltola , fighting to flip the Senate seat the majority runs through. Peggy Flanagan , one race from becoming the first Native American woman ever to serve in the Senate. Deb Haaland , running to govern the very state that barred her people from voting until 1948 — as the first Native American woman elected governor anywhere. Sharice Davids and Claire Valdez , fighting for the House seats a Democratic majority needs. Five Indigenous women. The Senate, the House, and a governorship. # PRESS RELEASE

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
October 30, 2026

**CONTACT**
Todd Cheewing
Todd@Ascent-Strategic.com

**LILY4CONGRESS CAMPAIGN FEATURES OVER 100 NEW HAMPSHIRE VETERANS WHO ENDORSE LILY TANG WILLIAMS FOR CONGRESS** **_With Election Day Just Four Days Away, Williams Highlights Strong Support from Granite Staters Who Served Our Nation_** WEARE, NH — With just four days until Election Day, Republican congressional nominee Lily Tang Williams is featuring more than 100 New Hampshire veterans who have officially endorsed her campaign for Congress in New Hampshire's Second Congressional District. The endorsements represent veterans from across the Granite State who have served our country and are standing behind Williams' candidacy.
[**SEE THE FULL LIST (CLICK HERE)**](https://us.list-manage.com/O2AzH8NA38D?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c)
“I am deeply honored to have the support of more than 100 Granite State veterans who put their lives on the line to defend our freedoms,” said Williams. “As someone who grew up under communist tyranny, I understand just how precious those freedoms are. These brave men and women fought to protect the American Dream, and I will never stop fighting to preserve it for future generations.” Lily Tang Williams emphasized her commitment to ensuring veterans receive the benefits, healthcare, and respect they have earned through their service, while holding Washington accountable for fulfilling its promises to those who wore our nation's uniform. “Our veterans deserve more than empty promises from Washington politicians,” Williams added. “They deserve a representative who will stand up for them, fight for their interests, and always put America first. I am humbled by their trust and proud to have them standing with me as we head into Election Day.” Williams enters the final four days of her campaign against incumbent Democrat Maggie Goodlander, continuing to emphasize affordability, accountability, and protecting the freedoms that make America exceptional — the ones these veterans have fought so hard to protect.

**About Lily Tang Williams**
Born in China just before Mao’s Cultural Revolution to working-class parents, Lily Tang Williams immigrated to the United States with nothing and built a life as an entrepreneur, educator, and community leader in Weare, NH. A living embodiment of the American Dream, she brings a uniquely powerful perspective to the fight for freedom and limited government.

In 2024, Williams won the Republican nomination and captured 47% of the general election vote against current incumbent Maggie Goodlander — coming closer than any Republican has in more than a decade to flipping NH-02. She is back and running stronger than ever in 2026.

You’ve heard it before: we must take action because democracy is at risk.
Donald Trump and his Republican allies have tried to manipulate elections. They know the playbook: voter suppression, election denial, intimidation at the polls, and gerrymandering. Put them together, and we steadily lose the ability to control our own futures.
But we are not afraid. This is a moment to channel outrage into action. And that is exactly how the Fair Fight team defends democracy.
I founded Fair Fight to advance voting rights after the 2018 election. When I saw eligible voters facing inexcusable barriers, I refused to be silent. I knew we needed a new coalition of patriots who would insist that every eligible voter can register to vote, cast their ballot, and have that ballot count.
Since then, the Fair Fight team has fought to protect those pillars of free and fair elections.
And in the run-up to Tuesday’s elections, they’ve strategically invested in races that are vital for turning back the tide on rising autocracy.
They’re fighting to flip the Georgia State House from red to blue, which is finally within reach after years of laying the groundwork. And they're fighting to elect Southern Democracy Champions to Congress who’ve stood up to new gerrymanders this year — and will keep fighting for fair maps and voting rights in Washington.
But these elections are hotly contested, and there’s a real chance we could fall just short of crucial victories. If MAGA Republicans cling to power, they will try to make that power permanent through more voter suppression and map-rigging. This is a pivot point for democracy — it could go either way.
[I’m asking you to donate to Fair Fight today because it would make a meaningful difference to elect Democracy Champions and preserve our freedoms.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142508498/657180554/-1736262579?refcode=emm_ff_20261030_SYA_v1s3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ZGM2MzYzNi02YWQ0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=UPwt9ouWkb2CkGV0HdVRCpksjXPBgyPwGXkjHkAYpCE=)
Protecting free and fair elections is not a spectator sport. It is a commitment that requires everyday action. Fair Fight refuses to stop defending your right to vote, and they will keep expanding access to the democracy we all deserve.
Thank you,
Stacey Abrams

Election Day is almost here — but Fair Fight’s monthly fundraising deadline will arrive even sooner at midnight tomorrow. And they need our support as they marshall resources to power a proven model of voter outreach, education, and protection for critical races up and down the ballot. = If you've saved payment info with ActBlue Express, your donation will process automatically: | = | = ---|--- = | = ---|--- = | = ---|--- You’ve heard it before: we must take action because democracy is at risk. Donald Trump and his Republican allies have tried to manipulate elections. They know the playbook: voter suppression, election denial, intimidation at the polls, and gerrymandering. Put them together, and we steadily lose the ability to control our own futures. But we are not afraid. This is a moment to channel outrage into action. And that is exactly how the Fair Fight team defends democracy. I founded Fair Fight to advance voting rights after the 2018 election. When I saw eligible voters facing inexcusable barriers, I refused to be silent. I knew we needed a new coalition of patriots who would insist that every eligible voter can register to vote, cast their ballot, and have that ballot count. Since then, the Fair Fight team has fought to protect those pillars of free and fair elections. And in the run-up to Tuesday’s elections, they’ve strategically invested in races that are vital for turning back the tide on rising autocracy. They’re fighting to flip the Georgia State House from red to blue, which is finally within reach after years of laying the groundwork. And they're fighting to elect Southern Democracy Champions to Congress who’ve stood up to new gerrymanders this year — and will keep fighting for fair maps and voting rights in Washington. But these elections are hotly contested, and there’s a real chance we could fall just short of crucial victories. If MAGA Republicans cling to power, they will try to make that power permanent through more voter suppression and map-rigging. This is a pivot point for democracy — it could go either way. = Protecting free and fair elections is not a spectator sport. It is a commitment that requires everyday action. Fair Fight refuses to stop defending your right to vote, and they will keep expanding access to the democracy we all deserve. Folks,
What a race it's been so far.
Since the start of early voting, our team and volunteers contacted more than 619,000 voters across North Carolina. And this week, I continued my Make Stuff Cost Less tour in Charlotte and Durham and felt the energy of a crowd ready for change and excited to cast their ballots.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/59604282-1ee3-4fe3-8ffc-bf5d31f5ffbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I launched this race last July because I knew that we could have better days ahead of us. And these past 15 months have shown me that North Carolinians agree. People all across the state and country are standing up and making their voices heard. They recognize that the chaos and corruption coming out of Washington DC is hurting their families and their communities and we have a crucial opportunity on Tuesday to vote for change.
That's the reason I'm in this race and why I'm still out here every day, talking with folks all across the state about how Washington can better serve them. Not the other way around.
Now, we're almost at the finish line.
**Tomorrow is the last day to vote early in person**. Find your early voting site [here](https://substack.com/redirect/c792c420-1dbb-4107-87c5-a2b3ec6ecb10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). If you've already voted, thank you! Reach out to a friend or family member today and help them make a plan to vote.
**Tomorrow is also the last day to register to vote if you haven 't yet.** In North Carolina, you can register and vote on the same day during early voting, but after that, you have to be registered to vote on Election Day. So if you haven't registered yet, find your local early voting site and register by tomorrow!
**Election day is on Tuesday.** If you can't make it tomorrow, polls are open on Tuesday, November 3rd from 6:30am to 7:30pm. Find your Election Day polling place [here](https://substack.com/redirect/c39665f6-14f9-41ed-b3e8-381171f02b77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
We have four more days to reach every voter in the state and make sure they have a plan to vote. **[Please, will you chip in $5 today and fuel our final organizing efforts so we can flip this crucial seat and take back the U.S. Senate to provide a course correction for our great country?](https://substack.com/redirect/59604282-1ee3-4fe3-8ffc-bf5d31f5ffbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/59604282-1ee3-4fe3-8ffc-bf5d31f5ffbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for being a part of this fight.
Thank you.

name: James Talarico
subject: Going for broke
body:
[1]Talarico for Texas

We’re going for broke.

As someone who cares about taking back Texas, you deserve transparency.

When we talked about our closing strategy and our budget, we knew that
putting more resources into getting out our message and mobilizing voters
would make a significant impact on Tuesday. The race is going to be close,
and we can’t leave any stone unturned.

So late last night, I gave my team the green light to spend every dollar
we have — to get as close to $0 in our bank account as we can stomach.
Don’t wait until tomorrow or Tuesday — do it now.

Leaving a single dollar unspent and coming up short by a few votes would
be devastating. Folks put their faith in us to use every resource
available, and I take the responsibility very seriously.

We had to move fast because the sooner we can start spending, the more
Texans we can reach before they vote.

It was a risk. But I took a leap of faith and put my trust in you because
I have seen what this team is capable of.

have the resources to win without making any cuts to our budget. Every
dollar will be spent winning votes and getting us across the finish line
on Tuesday.

If you've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution
instantly.

Let me be clear: This does not mean we have fully funded our campaign.
Exactly the opposite.

We have expenses and bills that we know are still coming. We, of course,
have to ensure our staff gets paid. So we have to raise all of that money
still — or else we’ll be looking at a bunch of disastrous last-minute
budget cuts come Monday.

But the risk was worth it. We can’t flip Texas by playing it safe, and it
would be an insult to everyone who has invested their time and money into
this movement to leave a bunch of money in the bank and come up short.

So yes, we spent more than we had in the budget, and we have a very short
window to refill our coffers because as it stands now...we’re broke.

Dream In the go-big-or-go-home collective consciousness of Texas, no
ambition is deemed too reckless, no daydream too wild. Save perhaps one.
It is the idea, fantastical to many as it is irresistible to others, that
the Democrats will win a statewide race in Texas for the first time in 32
years. According to the latest New York Times/Siena University poll of the
race for U.S. Senate, James Talarico, a 37-year-old state legislator seen

general, by six points. The poll was conducted from Sept. 21 to Sept. 30.
