also showed the Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Gina Hinojosa, four
points ahead of the three-term G.O.P. incumbent, Greg Abbott, the most
dominant political figure in Texas. Cue the fluttering heartbeats. Cue, as
well, the eye-rolls. Given how thoroughly Republicans have dominated the
state, and how the hopes of Democrats have repeatedly crashed, some Texas
pollsters remain skeptical. “At some point, you do get conditioned by all
that’s happened in the past,” said James Henson, the director of the
University of Texas at Austin’s Texas Politics Project. “I mean, you look
at the trends and you have to admit that something’s going on. But you
still don’t want to believe your lying eyes, because you’ve been burned
for so long.” Mr. Henson was referring to the perennial spectacle of
much-ballyhooed Texas Democratic aspirants face-planting against the Lone
Star State’s red wall. First came Tony Sanchez Jr., the swaggering and
self-funding Laredo oilman whom Gov. Rick Perry dispatched in 2002 by an
18-point margin. Next was the state senator Wendy Davis, who attracted
worldwide attention for her filibuster in the Texas Legislature against an
anti-abortion measure but whom Mr. Abbott demolished by 20 points in 2014.
Finally, the El Paso congressman Beto O’Rourke came up 2.6 points short of
defeating Senator Ted Cruz in 2018 but then suffered a 10-point loss to
Mr. Abbott four years later. Even with the awareness of such humiliations,
Democrats find themselves maintaining that 2026 could, at long last, be
the year. President Trump’s deep unpopularity and the prospect of a blue
wave could, they insist, extend into the state he won by nearly 14 points
in 2024. According to a September survey conducted by Texas Southern
University, Mr. Trump is seven points underwater in Texas. Mr. Talarico
has run an energetic and well-financed campaign, while Mr. Paxton has
staged far fewer public events and has had to rely on outside groups to
fund an attack-ad blitzkrieg against his Democratic opponent. Mr. Abbott,
meanwhile, has outspent Ms. Hinojosa by a 10-to-one ratio, yet has been
unable to build an insurmountable lead. “People have vastly underestimated
Gina,” said Ms. Davis, now a political consultant and a senior adviser to
Planned Parenthood Texas Votes, an advocacy organization. “Dollar for
dollar, she’s running the best statewide campaign we’ve ever seen.” Such
optimism stands in defiance of the political axiom that Texas is where
idealistic Democrats go to be mugged by reality. The party’s demise there
is not a product of ill fortune, Mr. Henson said. “Governor Abbott has
built an impressive election machine that has benefited state-level
Republicans again and again for a decade and a half,” he said. “And the
Democratic machinery here is almost nonexistent.” A ‘Hollowing-Out’ I have
written about the politics of my native state at regular intervals for
more than three decades. After watching the Democrats’ century-long rule
in Texas come to a decisive end with Gov. Ann Richards’s loss to George W.
Bush in 1994, I saw the party descend into atrophy in which failure begot
more failure. “The 30-year drought has done a lot of things,” said Luke
Warford, the chairman of the Travis County Democratic Party and the
founder of the Agave Democratic Infrastructure Fund. “It’s kept donors on
the sidelines, which makes a lot of potentially good candidates not run
because there’s no belief they can win. And it also makes a lot of really
talented staff leave to find better-paying work in true battleground
states.” The Democratic Party has no counterpart to Mr. Abbott, and hasn’t
since 1993, when Senator Lloyd Bentsen moved to Washington to join
President Bill Clinton’s cabinet. Its weaknesses are even more glaring
farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of
state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s
county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left
unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating
budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s
been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the
satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a
century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence
among the state’s ruling party. The party’s rightward tilt, increasingly
forceful with each legislative session, reached its apotheosis in March,
with Mr. Paxton’s primary victory over the more moderate Republican
four-term incumbent, Senator John Cornyn. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr.
Trump’s, was impeached by the Republican-controlled State House (and later
acquitted by the State Senate) in 2023 over allegations that included
bribery. He was also accused by his wife of adultery. Mr. Trump endorsed
him anyway, all but guaranteeing his landslide primary triumph over Mr.
Cornyn but in the process testing the allegiance of center-right Texans.
In similar fashion, the Texas G.O.P. is in danger of losing many Latino
voters who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024 after years of siding with
Democrats. “We adopted a lazy way of campaigning that bit us on the ass,
and we’ve learned from that,” Mr. O’Rourke said. “Now it’s the Republicans
who’ve gotten really lazy and complacent and comfortable.” Signs of
Republican Overreach Simply spending one week driving through the vastness
of Texas, as I did in September, is all it takes to appreciate an underdog
party’s uphill battle. The state’s 32 million residents are spread across
20 media markets, many of them distinct ecosystems, from the urban colossi
of Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex to the oil patch of the
Texas Panhandle to the Latino-dominated borderlands of the Rio Grande
Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a
place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine
Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by
the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at
the bottom of their list. It’s just so damned big.” Reaching so many
markets presents a daunting challenge for an upstart candidate like Ms.
Hinojosa, a state representative from the border city of Brownsville.
“There’s still 20 percent of the electorate that doesn’t know who I am,”
she said in an interview in mid-September. To date, Ms. Hinojosa’s
campaign has said that it has raised about $20 million. For his part, Mr.
Talarico spent about $30 million earlier this year to introduce himself
statewide as a man of Christian faith and a member of the Texas House with
a record of supporting bipartisan legislation. Since that time, however,
Mr. Paxton and his associates have invested more than $100 million in an
effort to redefine his opponent as “radical” and “weird,” with ads that
quote from remarks Mr. Talarico made several years ago (and later
renounced) suggesting that “God is nonbinary” and that there are six
biological sexes. Mr. Paxton and his allies have at times questioned Mr.
Talarico’s manhood and even his Christianity, an effort to jolt the
sensibilities of a state prone to mythologizing godly and masculine
archetypes. “How they’re negatively defining Talarico is kind of a
bank-shot way of saying that he’s not a true Texas conservative,” Mr.
Henson said. Whether money can overwhelm conditions on the ground is the
riddle looming over the Texas races. In the border city of Laredo, which
Mr. Trump won in 2024 — the first time a Republican had done so in over a
century — signs of buyer’s remorse are evident. Arrests by Immigration and
Customs Enforcement agents in Laredo were higher in July than in any other
American city. Mr. Trump’s erratic trade policies have further created
instability at the city’s port of entry. While acknowledging the economic
concerns that many border residents share, Adrian Zapata, a business
executive in the health industry who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, said in
an interview that the negative ads against Mr. Talarico were resonating
with some of his family members. “They see Talarico as an ultraliberal,”
he said. “They’re done with the ‘they/them.’ They’re going to vote for
Paxton just because of that.” As for Mr. Zapata, “I’m not ready to vote
for Talarico,” he said. “But I don’t like Paxton. He’s never done anything
for South Texas, and his personal and business dealings have hurt him a
lot with folks down here.” There is a similarly muddled electoral picture
in the cattle country of deep West Texas adjacent to Big Bend National
Park. Mr. Trump and Mr. Abbott have aggressively championed a border wall
and artificial intelligence data centers, both of which threaten to
disrupt the region’s pastoral ethos. A coalition of more than 200
landowners has sued the federal government over the border wall, while
other residents have circulated a petition to protest the construction of
a new data center near Fort Stockton. George Johnson, a cattle feed
operator in Alpine, waved off such concerns, saying: “Folks worrying about
data centers were also worried when the internet got started. It’s
Talarico who scares me to death, him and all that socialist talk.” Others
in this largely conservative region harbor the view that Republicans have
failed to make good on their promises. Thaddeus Cleveland, the Republican
sheriff of Terrell County, said that both he and his county had voted for
Mr. Trump in 2024, but added, “Everything he campaigned on, we’re seeing
the opposite of, like going to war.” Sheriff Cleveland predicted that the
negative campaign ads by the Republicans would not factor as significantly
into the votes of his neighbors as “the price of groceries and gas, which
are compounded here because we’re so far from everywhere else.” But it is
in purple Tarrant County, dominated by Fort Worth, where the party could
pay the price for having potentially overestimated its mandate from the
voters. Conservative leaders have cut funds for nonprofits that aid
at-risk children, subjected school library books to right-wing litmus
tests and eliminated free bus rides to polling stations in poor
neighborhoods. “The far-right leaders here have implemented Project 2025
on a county level,” said Alisa Simmons, a Democrat and county commissioner
who is running to unseat the conservative county judge, Tim O’Hare. In an
early sign this year that area Republicans may be out of step with Tarrant
County’s constituents, a Democratic aviation machinist and union leader,
Taylor Rehmet, defeated Leigh Wambsganss, a well-funded Republican
Christian activist who led the conservative takeover of several metroplex
school boards. He won by 14 points in a January special election for a
State Senate seat covering a region that Mr. Trump won by 17 points in
2024. A ‘Gradualist’ Theory Which party prevails in Texas is a complicated
riddle. Historically a low-turnout state — it ranked second to last in the
2024 election, ahead of only Arkansas — Texas held a primary in March that
saw nearly one in four voters showing up to the polls, a modern record for
midterm participation, with Democrats slightly outpacing Republicans. A
few factors could conspire to thwart a blue wave in Texas. As of 2020,
straight-ticket voting is no longer possible in the state, which could
impact the mostly Democratic urban counties where that practice has
frequently been used by voters in past elections. Texas is one of only
eight states that lack universal online registration, while voting by mail
is also highly restricted. In January, Mr. Abbott turned over the state’s
list of approximately 18.7 million registered voters to the Trump
administration, and 1.2 million of them have subsequently been put on the
“suspense list” because their addresses have not been verified. The recent
shuttering of nearly one-third of Tarrant County’s polling sites by its
Republican-controlled county commission is particularly worrisome for
Democrats. “The reason we’ve lost these statewide races in the past is
because we’ve never gotten enough out of Tarrant County to overcome the
margins in rural Texas,” Ms. Davis said of the turnout. “If we don’t get
it to 53 or 54 percent this November, it’s game over. James and Gina can’t
win.” But the state’s Republicans have reasons of their own to be fretful.
Partly because of the recruitment efforts of the Texas Majority PAC and
Blueprint Texas, a down-ballot candidate support organization co-founded
by Ms. Davis earlier this year, the Democrats are fielding a full slate in
all 150 state races for the first time in a half-century. Though many of
these aspirants face long odds, their presence on the ballot could
energize the Democrats in predominantly conservative regions who have not
bothered to turn out in the past. “If we win on Nov. 3, most of those
names running down-ballot in really tough areas like East Texas and the
Hill Country and the Panhandle will be responsible,” Mr. O’Rourke said.
Mr. Henson added that while he remained skeptical about Democratic
enthusiasm being sufficient to carry the day for Mr. Talarico, he also
doubted that a last-minute avalanche of negative ads would prove decisive
for Mr. Paxton. “At a certain point, there’s diminishing impact once you
get past an absurd level of spending,” he said. Rather than project a
winner in November, Mr. Henson said he felt more comfortable embracing a
“gradualist” theory, one in which Texas does not become blue overnight,
but instead competitive. “Even if Talarico loses by a Beto-like margin,”
he said, “the next cycle is a presidential election, where Trump likely
won’t be popular and Democratic turnout will be higher. So there are
reasons for Texas Democrats to be optimistic.”'

Greg Abbott has been caught in yet another lie, and this time, the receipts are coming straight from his own administration.
Last month, Abbott announced a so-called "pause" on data center permits, pretending to take action against the very corporations he invited into our communities with the richest tax breaks in the country.
**But new reporting revealed that Texas regulators approved 35 permits related to data center projects AFTER Abbott ordered his supposed pause. It 's crystal clear that this "pause" was a stunt meant to help Abbott score political points with the very communities he's already sold out.**
It's too late for Abbott to change loyalties now. He's married to monied special interests and has no commitment to the people of Texas, which is why he never bothered to enforce his own directive.
If Greg Abbott was committed to protecting Texas communities from the unchecked expansion of data centers, he would have taken me up on my call for a special legislative session to pass real laws that protect our communities and establish clear standards for how data center projects are approved and built.
While Abbott was telling Texans he was cracking down on data centers, his own administration was quietly allowing them to move forward.
Meanwhile, working Texans are left to deal with the consequences.
From Dallas to rural communities across our state, families have rightfully raised concerns about data centers threatening their water supply, straining our already fragile power grid, and moving into their neighborhoods without their input.
The question we should all be asking ourselves is **" When are we -- the people of Texas -- going to be included in the conversation on data centers?"**
My answer -- _when I 'm the Governor of Texas._ Texans deserve a seat at the table to decide IF and HOW data centers come into their community. Texans will get that power when I am governor.
**We can 't trust the arsonist to put out the fire. Greg Abbott took $22.5 million from data center interests, allowed 596 data centers to be planned or built across Texas, and then announced a fake pause to save his political career.**
_It 's time we object._
With Election Day just FOUR days away, we have a chance to put an end to Abbott's pay-to-play politics and elect a governor who answers to working Texans, not billionaire corporations.
**[I'm on the ground mobilizing voters, and we still have a lot of ground to cover. Will you please chip in $5 or whatever you can today to help us defeat Greg Abbott and elect a governor who will finally put Texans first?](https://substack.com/redirect/b6f50719-023f-4c71-a40b-33f9abfcd5f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE ->](https://substack.com/redirect/b6f50719-023f-4c71-a40b-33f9abfcd5f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Let's put an end to Abbott's data center madness.
-- Gina Hinojosa

body:
It’s a risk, yes. But I’ve taken bigger risks before.
#

Friend —
It’s Gabby. I had to make a tough call this morning, and I wanted you to hear about it from me.
Yesterday, our team showed me a plan to reach what might be an election-deciding amount of undecided voters in Michigan, Ohio, and Texas this weekend. The last weekend before Election Day.
The issue is, we don’t have the money for it yet. We’ve committed $10 million already, which is a significant amount for us. But this morning, I made a difficult decision.
I said yes anyway.
It’s a risk, yes. But I’ve taken bigger risks before. I ran for Congress, I fought back after I was shot, I learned to walk again, to speak again, one word at a time. I know what it means to refuse to give up.
Many of our races are close. A few hundred votes could decide who controls Congress and whether gun safety moves forward or backward for years to come.
So, I’m counting on you now. We need to raise everything we can to fully fund this plan before our end-of-month deadline tomorrow at midnight.

name: Lily Tomlin (via JanePAC.com)
subject: what I admire most about Jane
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee
body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=12%2E6803%2Ev2N5mt)
It's Lily.
Jane and I have been friends for more than fifty years, which means we've been through just about everything, from protests and arrests at the steps of the Capitol to award shows and more _Grace and Frankie_ rehearsals than I could possibly count.
Sometimes the night ends with Jane sitting in my lap 😂.
[](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261030-ak.Kbs5jZ&refcode=em20261030-12&t=3&akid=12%2E6803%2Ev2N5mt)
Through all those years, one thing about Jane has never changed: **she never gets tired of fighting for what she believes in — for what she knows in her heart is _right._**
And you and I both know what is happening in our country right now is _not_ right.
Jane sees it. I see it. But instead of enjoying retirement like the rest of us, Jane is doing whatever she can to help elect the kinds of leaders who will fight for a dignified future for everyone who calls this country home.
**[Now I'm asking you to help: Jane's team needs to raise $50,000 in grassroots online donations before their fundraising deadline on October 31 at midnight. Will you chip in whatever you can to help them head into the final 4 days until Election Day with undeniable people power?](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261030-ak.Kbs5jZ&amount=5&refcode=em20261030-12&t=4&akid=12%2E6803%2Ev2N5mt)**
I'll admit it: even I've been amazed watching this movement grow.
_More than 250 climate leaders elected across the country._ Every one of those victories means another person in office willing to stand up to the fossil fuel industry and fight for clean air, drinkable water, and a democracy that actually answers to the people.
That’s the kind of future Jane and I have been fighting for since our _9 to 5 days_.
**And somehow — even with an egotistical bigot-in-chief doing his damnedest to drag us backward — that future is becoming more and more possible because people like you keep showing up.**
But we cannot lose sight of what’s ahead.
This year, Jane and her team have watched polluters and corporate super PACs spend massive sums against their endorsed candidates. We know the lies will only get louder, and the checks will only grow larger.
Over the next 4 days, we need to help these candidates knock on doors, make calls, and reach voters to compete with Big Oil and the powerful interests trying to drown them out.
That's not something Jane takes lightly, and neither do I.
**[So I’m asking you to help Jane’s team finish the election strong with a donation of any amount today. I’m immensely grateful for your support.](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261030-ak.Kbs5jZ&amount=5&refcode=em20261030-12&t=5&akid=12%2E6803%2Ev2N5mt)**

Let's keep this going.
Lily

Hey, friend, Senator Mark Kelly from Arizona here with a message I need you to see.
I was just in New Mexico campaigning with Deb Haaland in the final stretch of her race for Governor. This race matters, and after spending the day with Deb and the voters she’s fighting for, I'm more certain than ever that she is the right person for the job.

**_[If you’re with us, will you chip in $5 right now to help elect Deb Haaland as New Mexico’s next Governor?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1703-fr-nd&amount=5&t=3&akid=13593%2E400544%2E-V-stM)_**

Friend, I've spent my career focused on service, solving problems, and getting things done: as a Navy pilot, as a NASA astronaut, and now in the U.S. Senate.
**Deb works the same way.** New Mexico families are struggling with rising costs. They're worried about their access to healthcare, the future of their public schools, and whether their kids will have the same opportunities they had. Deb is running to tackle those problems head-on as Governor, and working families know they can count on her to have their back.

Arizona and New Mexico share a border, but we share a lot more than that: workers, businesses, public lands, and communities feeling the same squeeze. When New Mexico has a Governor focused on lowering costs and expanding opportunity, our whole region is stronger.

**FRIDAY, OCTOBER 30, 2026**
**John Adams | Letter to Abigail Adams, October 13, 1775**
"Pray my dear cherish in the Minds of my Nabby and Johnny and Charly and Tommy the Remembrance of their Grand mamma, and remind them of her Precepts and Example."
John Adams wrote these words to Abigail after the death of her mother. He had seen how much their children's grandmother had contributed to their upbringing, and he did not want her influence to end with her absence.
We know that those we love will not always be beside us. Yet something of them may remain in the lessons they taught, the care they gave, and the example they set.
What do we carry forward from those who helped shape us?
**Pause.
Breath.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

**A SWEET GROUND INVITATION**
In Sweet Ground, we reflect on the people who shape us, the choices we make, what we must sometimes unlearn, and what we carry forward.
Now, I would like to hear from you.
Is there a moment from your own life that has stayed with you? Something a parent or grandparent taught you, a conversation you never forgot, a lesson you understood only years later, or an ordinary moment that turned out not to be so ordinary?
**Share your Sweet Ground moment in the comments.** A few words are enough. A memory, a story, even a photograph with a few words about what it means to you.
There is no right answer and no perfect story. Just something from your life that you carry with you.
I would love to hear it.

clean_body: The lives that continue to shape our own. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The lives that continue to shape our own. | | | Oct 30 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- FRIDAY, OCTOBER 30, 2026 John Adams | Letter to Abigail Adams, October 13, 1775 "Pray my dear cherish in the Minds of my Nabby and Johnny and Charly and Tommy the Remembrance of their Grand mamma, and remind them of her Precepts and Example." John Adams wrote these words to Abigail after the death of her mother. He had seen how much their children's grandmother had contributed to their upbringing, and he did not want her influence to end with her absence. We know that those we love will not always be beside us. Yet something of them may remain in the lessons they taught, the care they gave, and the example they set. What do we carry forward from those who helped shape us? Pause. Breath. Look Deeper. Refuel. Welcome to Sweet Ground. | | ---|---|--- A SWEET GROUND INVITATION In Sweet Ground, we reflect on the people who shape us, the choices we make, what we must sometimes unlearn, and what we carry forward. Now, I would like to hear from you. Is there a moment from your own life that has stayed with you? Something a parent or grandparent taught you, a conversation you never forgot, a lesson you understood only years later, or an ordinary moment that turned out not to be so ordinary? Share your Sweet Ground moment in the comments. A few words are enough. A memory, a story, even a photograph with a few words about what it means to you. There is no right answer and no perfect story. Just something from your life that you carry with you. I would love to hear it. Dear Patriot,
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckb2O2zAQhJ-G6mSQXP3YhYoAhrtLm1JYL5cSYVIUyNUd8vaBHFyZJuXOzgzwYX59zB8YYtiWn5h4KuLnUuct04pF6paXkFKgV125cJV1ttoOrdEt6BlJwifPHTZucuTQUMOTGW8Aox5M36yTvaL3ntB3w3Vwt6sbb3Ykq53uyWvkJkxnn9GgTQfawAWu_DQ0WjTgoTe96jRGLnIpvB_PGAg3wfryuRBfKKcmTqvIXhX8UPah7KMyHYUvuLHLcjqUfeQXs-fELuBS8rGfUlrarxWlDdIiyYEx_m4pV6lterZ73lHB45A013wUYgX3fyeUHU7n2X8kBfd3-q9GmHYMy6bg_g36_cmb8CYK7kW8sgOmfLxP6Jsyuf0rxBjqMKpOLwlDfMPKf-7zOdk_AQAA__9FPaTS)People ask me where the money goes. It is a fair question, and I am going to answer it plainly, without a chart and without any gimmick. First, let me describe what I am **not** going to do. I am not going to tell you that thirty-five dollars buys one specific thing. You have received that email from other organizations. **It is not how any of this works, and I will not put a number on a page just because it sounds good.** Here is what actually happens when I open an operation. **Somebody has to physically get there.** Not somewhere nearby. Directly there. When a United States Senator told the Senate floor that island voters would have to spend **eleven hundred dollars a seat** flying to Anchorage to prove citizenship, do you know who ended up buying that ticket? **I did.** That was one seat, one leg, one story, and it is the only reason anyone knows her claim did not hold up. **Somebody has to have a vehicle.** Not a rideshare. An actual rental. You do not want a permanent record of every address your team visited sitting on somebody else's server. **Somebody has to sleep somewhere.** For as long as the story requires, not for as long as the budget allows. A source who finally agrees to talk on the fourth day does not care that we only booked three nights. **Then there is fuel, and there is equipment.** Cameras fail, cameras get discovered, and cameras get confiscated. They all have to be replaced, and the replacements are expensive. **[Every one of those is being spent right now, in two states, by two different teams.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckb2O2zAQhJ-G6mSQXP3YhYoAhrtLm1JYL5cSYVIUyNUd8vaBHFyZJuXOzgzwYX59zB8YYtiWn5h4KuLnUuct04pF6paXkFKgV125cJV1ttoOrdEt6BlJwifPHTZucuTQUMOTGW8Aox5M36yTvaL3ntB3w3Vwt6sbb3Ykq53uyWvkJkxnn9GgTQfawAWu_DQ0WjTgoTe96jRGLnIpvB_PGAg3wfryuRBfKKcmTqvIXhX8UPah7KMyHYUvuLHLcjqUfeQXs-fELuBS8rGfUlrarxWlDdIiyYEx_m4pV6lterZ73lHB45A013wUYgX3fyeUHU7n2X8kBfd3-q9GmHYMy6bg_g36_cmb8CYK7kW8sgOmfLxP6Jsyuf0rxBjqMKpOLwlDfMPKf-7zOdk_AQAA__9FPaTS)** **[FUND THE OPERATION — CHIP IN $35](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckb2O2zAQhJ-G6mSQXP3YhYoAhrtLm1JYL5cSYVIUyNUd8vaBHFyZJuXOzgzwYX59zB8YYtiWn5h4KuLnUuct04pF6paXkFKgV125cJV1ttoOrdEt6BlJwifPHTZucuTQUMOTGW8Aox5M36yTvaL3ntB3w3Vwt6sbb3Ykq53uyWvkJkxnn9GgTQfawAWu_DQ0WjTgoTe96jRGLnIpvB_PGAg3wfryuRBfKKcmTqvIXhX8UPah7KMyHYUvuLHLcjqUfeQXs-fELuBS8rGfUlrarxWlDdIiyYEx_m4pV6lterZ73lHB45A013wUYgX3fyeUHU7n2X8kBfd3-q9GmHYMy6bg_g36_cmb8CYK7kW8sgOmfLxP6Jsyuf0rxBjqMKpOLwlDfMPKf-7zOdk_AQAA__9FPaTS)** And there is one more line, the one nobody outside this building ever thinks about. **An attorney reviews the footage before it airs.** Every frame, every single time. That is not simply caution for its own sake. That review is why our work survives when they come for it, and they always come for it. It is also why a federal appeals court could look at what we do and call it protected journalism. **Nothing we publish is worth the newsroom that publishes it.** So the lawyer gets paid, every single time, before you ever see a second of video. **[That is the whole honest list. Nothing hidden in it.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckb2O2zAQhJ-G6mSQXP3YhYoAhrtLm1JYL5cSYVIUyNUd8vaBHFyZJuXOzgzwYX59zB8YYtiWn5h4KuLnUuct04pF6paXkFKgV125cJV1ttoOrdEt6BlJwifPHTZucuTQUMOTGW8Aox5M36yTvaL3ntB3w3Vwt6sbb3Ykq53uyWvkJkxnn9GgTQfawAWu_DQ0WjTgoTe96jRGLnIpvB_PGAg3wfryuRBfKKcmTqvIXhX8UPah7KMyHYUvuLHLcjqUfeQXs-fELuBS8rGfUlrarxWlDdIiyYEx_m4pV6lterZ73lHB45A013wUYgX3fyeUHU7n2X8kBfd3-q9GmHYMy6bg_g36_cmb8CYK7kW8sgOmfLxP6Jsyuf0rxBjqMKpOLwlDfMPKf-7zOdk_AQAA__9FPaTS)** **[YES — PUT MY GIFT STRAIGHT INTO THE FIELD](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckb2O2zAQhJ-G6mSQXP3YhYoAhrtLm1JYL5cSYVIUyNUd8vaBHFyZJuXOzgzwYX59zB8YYtiWn5h4KuLnUuct04pF6paXkFKgV125cJV1ttoOrdEt6BlJwifPHTZucuTQUMOTGW8Aox5M36yTvaL3ntB3w3Vwt6sbb3Ykq53uyWvkJkxnn9GgTQfawAWu_DQ0WjTgoTe96jRGLnIpvB_PGAg3wfryuRBfKKcmTqvIXhX8UPah7KMyHYUvuLHLcjqUfeQXs-fELuBS8rGfUlrarxWlDdIiyYEx_m4pV6lterZ73lHB45A013wUYgX3fyeUHU7n2X8kBfd3-q9GmHYMy6bg_g36_cmb8CYK7kW8sgOmfLxP6Jsyuf0rxBjqMKpOLwlDfMPKf-7zOdk_AQAA__9FPaTS)** Now here is the part I really need you to understand, because it is the reason for this email. **Those bills do not arrive on a schedule that matches your generosity.** The hotel bills tonight, the rental car bills tonight, and the airline was paid several weeks ago. The attorney's invoice arrives at the end of the month, regardless of whether we published anything at all. **Support tends to arrive after a video is published. For as long as the story requires, not for as long as the budget allows. A source who finally agrees to talk on the fourth day does not care that we only booked three nights. Then there is fuel, and there is equipment. Cameras fail, cameras get discovered, and cameras get confiscated. They all have to be replaced, and the replacements are expensive. And there is one more line, the one nobody outside this building ever thinks about. An attorney reviews the footage before it airs. Every frame, every single time. That is not simply caution for its own sake. That review is why our work survives when they come for it, and they always come for it. It is also why a federal appeals court could look at what we do and call it protected journalism. Nothing we publish is worth the newsroom that publishes it. So the lawyer gets paid, every single time, before you ever see a second of video. Now here is the part I really need you to understand, because it is the reason for this email. Those bills do not arrive on a schedule that matches your generosity. The hotel bills tonight, the rental car bills tonight, and the airline was paid several weeks ago. # **North Korean hackers steal $6.3B in largest crypto heist ever**
Hackers linked to North Korea's TraderTraitor group **[stole approximately $6.36 billion from Binance,](https://substack.com/redirect/86b4cee1-9b5f-42de-85b7-fada088fed22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, across ten blockchains, with most of the theft occurring in roughly 20 minutes, according to blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs, which expressed "high confidence" in the attribution.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/86b4cee1-9b5f-42de-85b7-fada088fed22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Binance said deposits remain unaffected and withdrawals are temporarily suspended;** the exchange has recovered or frozen about $3 billion so far and pledged to cover all remaining losses using company funds and its reserve fund.
* **The theft surpasses last year 's $1.5 billion Bybit hack, also attributed to North Korea,** making it the largest cryptocurrency theft on record; one industry insider called it "the largest bank heist in human history," while Binance said it's working with law enforcement to identify and prosecute those responsible.

# **El Salvador deploys over 2,000 troops to Haiti after soldier kidnapping**
President Nayib Bukele **[ordered a surge of over 2,000 Salvadoran troops,](https://substack.com/redirect/88748e9f-59c2-4117-b00d-c20b79525533?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** into Haiti after gangs ambushed and kidnapped four Salvadoran aviation technicians serving with a UN-backed gang suppression force on Oct. 18.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/88748e9f-59c2-4117-b00d-c20b79525533?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Bukele rejected claims by an NGO that four burned bodies belonged to the missing men,** citing inconsistencies, and insisted on social media the deployment isn't an invasion, saying El Salvador seeks only to recover its soldiers and confront the gangs responsible.
* **The operation lacks a signed status-of-forces agreement with Haiti,** raising legal questions from officials like former Haitian defense minister Jean Dorneval, as gang violence has killed over 5,700 people in Haiti this year amid an ongoing security crisis since President Jovenel Moise's 2021 assassination.

| Peter,

Most Americans support abortion rights, and voters keep proving it at the state level.

In 2024, seven states — Arizona, Colorado, Maryland, Missouri, Montana, Nevada, and New York — passed ballot measures protecting abortion and the right to reproductive freedom.

[On Tuesday, abortion is on the ballot again in four states.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/142519327/657197378/610965683?sourceid=1151700&utm_campaign=27emcus-1007aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=ballot&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NmJkOTQ3ZS03MGQ0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=EcMTzlAY1VKRPUXhMWB-oJLjCZF2EME3BGfKiYxaIbg=&emci=ad3f66e6-54d2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&emdi=66bd947e-70d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=954237) Voters in Idaho, Nevada, and Virginia can protect reproductive rights.Missouri voters are fighting off a measure that would bring back a near-total ban on abortion:
* **Idaho's Proposition 1 would establish a right to abortion** and to reproductive freedom and privacy in state law. It would overturn Idaho’s current abortion ban, which is so extreme that doctors have left the state in droves.
* **Missouri's Amendment 3 would repeal the voter-approved Right to Reproductive Freedom Amendment** and ban abortion with extremely limited exceptions. Missourians voted to protect abortion just two years ago.
* **Nevada's Question 6 would establish a fundamental right to abortion** in the state constitution. Voters approved it in 2024, but it must pass twice to take effect. This is the second and final vote.
* **Virginia's Question 1 would make reproductive freedom a fundamental right** in the state constitution, including abortion, contraception, fertility care, and maternal health care.

Abortion bans cause real harm. Since _Roe v. Wade_ fell in 2022, a chaotic patchwork of state laws has emboldened anti-abortion politicians to escalate their attacks.

Patients are airlifted out of state for emergency care. They're turned away from emergency rooms. Some are forced to stay pregnant, only to deliver stillborn babies.

On Tuesday, voters in these four states can give millions of people the power to control their lives, their bodies, and their health.

**Peter, your support powers the Center's fight to overturn abortion bans and protect reproductive care for everyone, no matter the outcome on Tuesday.**

Thank you for being our partner in this work.

Onward,

Nancy Northup

clean_body: Ballot measures to watch on Election Day | | | | | | Peter, Most Americans support abortion rights, and voters keep proving it at the state level. In 2024, seven states — Arizona, Colorado, Maryland, Missouri, Montana, Nevada, and New York — passed ballot measures protecting abortion and the right to reproductive freedom. Voters in Idaho, Nevada, and Virginia can protect reproductive rights.Missouri voters are fighting off a measure that would bring back a near-total ban on abortion: Idaho's Proposition 1 would establish a right to abortion and to reproductive freedom and privacy in state law. It would overturn Idaho’s current abortion ban, which is so extreme that doctors have left the state in droves. Missouri's Amendment 3 would repeal the voter-approved Right to Reproductive Freedom Amendment and ban abortion with extremely limited exceptions. Missourians voted to protect abortion just two years ago. Nevada's Question 6 would establish a fundamental right to abortion in the state constitution. Voters approved it in 2024, but it must pass twice to take effect. This is the second and final vote. Virginia's Question 1 would make reproductive freedom a fundamental right in the state constitution, including abortion, contraception, fertility care, and maternal health care. Abortion bans cause real harm. Since Roe v. Wade fell in 2022, a chaotic patchwork of state laws has emboldened anti-abortion politicians to escalate their attacks. Patients are airlifted out of state for emergency care. They're turned away from emergency rooms. Some are forced to stay pregnant, only to deliver stillborn babies. On Tuesday, voters in these four states can give millions of people the power to control their lives, their bodies, and their health. Peter, your support powers the Center's fight to overturn abortion bans and protect reproductive care for everyone, no matter the outcome on Tuesday. Thank you for being our partner in this work. Onward, Nancy Northup President & CEO | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|--- The Center for Reproductive Rights uses the power of law to advance reproductive rights as fundamental human rights around the world. © Center for Reproductive Rights Center for Reproductive Rights 199 Water St. New York, NY 10038 United States

Arecent poll from the New York Times has Susan Collins winning this race by three points.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1059c2b0-2012-40fe-bdae-45994863329e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
If you know me, you know I don't put much stock in a single poll. One poll is a snapshot on one timeframe with one sample of voters - it's no reason to panic.
### **But this close to this election, there are no flukes.**
So I'm not going to mince words with you. This is a five-alarm fire for our campaign.
Donald Trump and the billionaires funding Susan Collins are reading the same numbers I am.
Up until now, Maine was worth a lot to them. Now, it's worth even more.
Susan has been outspending us on TV. About 5% of Maine voters haven't made up their minds yet, and those voters are going to make up their minds based on what's on their screen in the next 4 days. Right now, she owns every piece of real estate on that screen.
That is the honest truth, because you deserve nothing less than it.
### **So here 's what we're doing about it.**
I've launched a same-day $1,000,000 goal. Not a week-long goal, not an end-of-month goal -- today.
If we hit it, we buy even more ads in the 4 days, and we reach those undecided voters. If we don't, our shot at flipping Maine -- and with it, the Senate majority -- starts to fade, and there is not much time left to get it back.
I've never needed your support more than I do right now. I've spent this whole campaign telling you that people like us can beat $114 million if enough of us show up. Today's the day that either turns out to be true or it doesn't.
**[Please don't wait to take action. Will you chip in any amount to help us reach our goal, defeat Susan Collins, and flip the Senate for Democrats?](https://substack.com/redirect/1059c2b0-2012-40fe-bdae-45994863329e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[FLIP THE SENATE ->](https://substack.com/redirect/1059c2b0-2012-40fe-bdae-45994863329e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Let's get to work,
Troy

I’ll keep this brief, Peter.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1789&source=&t=1&akid=5093%2E124072%2ERCz03n) | | | |

Peter,
With just one day left until our last end-of-month deadline before Election Day and a $5 million goal to reach, [**_I’m personally asking you to make your first donation to my campaign right away._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1789&amount=5&t=8&akid=5093%2E124072%2ERCz03n)
Back when I ran for Governor in 2016, all the numbers and polls seemed to be in our favor – but I ended up winning by just 0.22% of the vote, and President Trump carried North Carolina in the presidential election.
Ten years later, I’m up against his handpicked candidate in a race experts say could decide Senate control, and the predictions appear to be on our side once again.
**The GOP has spent millions to defeat me, and if I learned anything from 2016, it’s that we cannot take this race for granted.**
[**_Before our final end-of-month deadline before the election, will you chip in $5 for the first time to help power our critical get-out-the-vote efforts, flip this must-win seat and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1789&amount=5&t=9&akid=5093%2E124072%2ERCz03n)

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

name: David Hogg
subject: The last weekend
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
This is it, Peter. The last
weekend before Election Day — and tomorrow night is our final end-of-month
deadline before the polls close.

I’m incredibly grateful for everything you’ve done to power our work.
Every time you read these emails, pitch in a few dollars, and show up for
our endorsed candidates, you’re proving that people-powered politics can
take on corporate money and win. I see that energy firsthand on the ground
with our candidates every day, and it’s the reason we’ve made it this far.

I’ve been on the road nonstop this month:

In California, I rallied with Angela Gonzales-Torres, hit the doors with
Randy Villegas whose running to flip a seat that’s critical to taking back
the House, and got out the vote with Mai Vang, taking on a 48 year
political dynasty to finally deliver power back to the people of
Sacramento.

In Michigan, I was on the ground with Abdul El-Sayed, who’s in a dead heat
race for a U.S. Senate seat against Trump’s handpicked candidate, and
Katrina Manetta, running for a seat that’s one of our best shots to flip
the Michigan House, where Democrats are just four seats away from a
majority.

In Ohio, I rallied at Wright State University with Kristina Knickerbocker,
taking on a GOP incumbent in a race that could help decide control of the
House. I was also knocking doors with Laalitya Acharya, whose win will
keep Republicans further away from a supermajority in the state House.

And in Wisconsin, I campaigned with Trevor Jung, who's running in one of
the few seats that could flip the state Senate — Wisconsin Democrats
called this the “most flippable chamber in the country.”

My next stop is Florida, where our candidate Jane Aman is running in a
must-win flip district to bring Democrats within striking distance of
breaking the Republican supermajority in the state House.

The margins in these races will be razor thin,
Peter. In many of them, a few hundred votes could
decide who we’ll have to protect and defend us in Congress and statehouses
on abortion, healthcare, redistricting, economic security, and whether ICE
keeps terrorizing our communities.

That’s what tomorrow’s deadline is about. Getting the next generation of
bold, young progressive leaders across the finish line so they can show up
on Day One to fight for working families and put a real check on Trump’s
dangerous agenda. Every dollar we raise tonight will go right to work
fueling our final push. That means keeping ads on the air and getting our
candidates the support they need to reach as many undecided voters as
possible before the polls close on Tuesday.

This is what it all comes down to,
Peter. If you’ve been waiting for the right
moment to pitch in, we need you now:
[ https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261030_2_final.4V2NgV&refcode=em20261030-4209&amount=3&t=1001&akid=4209%2E587540%2E2e15iU ]https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_lwd_20261030_2_final

And if you’ve already given, from the bottom of my heart, THANK YOU!
You’re the reason we can continue this work. If you can, please match your
previous $3 donation to help us finish strong on Tuesday:
[ https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261030_2_final.4V2NgV&refcode=em20261030-4209&amount=3&t=1002&akid=4209%2E587540%2E2e15iU ]https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_lwd_20261030_2_final

I’m heading back out there now. Thank you for being in this with me —
let’s bring home these wins!

— David

clean_body: This is it, Peter. The last weekend before Election Day — and tomorrow night is our final end-of-month deadline before the polls close. I’m incredibly grateful for everything you’ve done to power our work. Every time you read these emails, pitch in a few dollars, and show up for our endorsed candidates, you’re proving that people-powered politics can take on corporate money and win. I see that energy firsthand on the ground with our candidates every day, and it’s the reason we’ve made it this far. I’ve been on the road nonstop this month: In California, I rallied with Angela Gonzales-Torres, hit the doors with Randy Villegas whose running to flip a seat that’s critical to taking back the House, and got out the vote with Mai Vang, taking on a 48 year political dynasty to finally deliver power back to the people of Sacramento. In Michigan, I was on the ground with Abdul El-Sayed, who’s in a dead heat race for a U.S. Senate seat against Trump’s handpicked candidate, and Katrina Manetta, running for a seat that’s one of our best shots to flip the Michigan House, where Democrats are just four seats away from a majority. In Ohio, I rallied at Wright State University with Kristina Knickerbocker, taking on a GOP incumbent in a race that could help decide control of the House. I was also knocking doors with Laalitya Acharya, whose win will keep Republicans further away from a supermajority in the state House. And in Wisconsin, I campaigned with Trevor Jung, who's running in one of the few seats that could flip the state Senate — Wisconsin Democrats called this the “most flippable chamber in the country.” My next stop is Florida, where our candidate Jane Aman is running in a must-win flip district to bring Democrats within striking distance of breaking the Republican supermajority in the state House. The margins in these races will be razor thin, Peter. In many of them, a few hundred votes could decide who we’ll have to protect and defend us in Congress and statehouses on abortion, healthcare, redistricting, economic security, and whether ICE keeps terrorizing our communities. That’s what tomorrow’s deadline is about. Getting the next generation of bold, young progressive leaders across the finish line so they can show up on Day One to fight for working families and put a real check on Trump’s dangerous agenda. Every dollar we raise tonight will go right to work fueling our final push. That means keeping ads on the air and getting our candidates the support they need to reach as many undecided voters as possible before the polls close on Tuesday. This is what it all comes down to, Peter. If you’ve been waiting for the right moment to pitch in, we need you now: [ ] And if you’ve already given, from the bottom of my heart, THANK YOU! You’re the reason we can continue this work. If you can, please match your previous $3 donation to help us finish strong on Tuesday: [ ] I’m heading back out there now. Thank you for being in this with me — let’s bring home these wins! — David

The Department of Justice is investigating CCTV video from Lewiston City Hall that appears to show dozens of instances of NGO workers -- operating as "interpreters" -- coaching illiterate Somalis on how to vote and even filling out ballots for them.
The shocking footage was obtained by The Maine Wire under the Freedom of Access Act and shows left-wing NGOs running an industrial-scale ballot stuffing scheme, using non-English-speaking migrants to obtain ballots and then instructing them on how to vote a party line ticket for Democrats.
"We review all evidence concerning complaints of voter intimidation and election interference, including the video from Lewiston's early voting at City Hall," U.S. Attorney for Maine Andrew Benson told _The Robinson Report._
"We will not tolerate threats to the integrity of our elections, and we look forward to working with the Attorney General's Office and the Secretary of State's office to defend our democracy," said Benson.

When videos and images showing irregular behavior by the alleged Somali translators first went viral last week, Lewiston Mayor Carl Sheline quickly moved to block photojournalists from documenting the violations election officials would later disrupt multiple times.
Sheline, who spent $40,000 of his own money to win the $7,000 mayoral job, has been an unambiguous devotee to the narrow agenda of the Darod/Ogaden clan of Somalis that dominates the migrant NGO world in Lewiston.
Carl Sheline, seen here posing with Graham Platner, posted a notice limiting photography after The Maine Wire caught "translators" seeming to violate Maine law.
Sheline's bid to limit journalists' ability to document election shenanigans, however, did not cover the city's own CCTV cameras, which captured 140 hours of electioneering so tawdry it would have made Boss Tweed blush.
The CCTV video was obtained under Maine's Freedom of Access Act and covers the period of [early in-person voting](https://substack.com/redirect/ef5831f7-4b8e-4a6f-9f3c-5e18ee6692c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at City Hall, which began on Oct. 13.
Lewiston has been in the national spotlight since _The Maine Wire_ published [photographs by reporter Jon Fetherston](https://substack.com/redirect/b6433f7b-78e4-47c5-bfd6-446deb43252e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The photos raised questions about whether the dozen or more Somali NGO staffers working the early voting room were translating ballots or coaching voters on how to vote for Democrats.

Under Maine law, voters may request a translator, but there are strict rules as to what aides can and cannot do when it comes to assisting voters. Translators are not allowed to offer assistance but must wait until assistance is requested, and they are not allowed to influence voters' choices. The translators are not allowed to mark up a ballot, and they cannot approach or interrupt a voter who is already in the booth.
As is evident from the CCTV video, virtually every one of these rules was violated over and over again by a small cadre of political activists who can be seen shepherding illiterate Somali voters through the ballot-casting process.
After the national attention on voting irregularities in Lewiston, the city clerk began disseminating a printout informing the Somali NGO staffers of the rules.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ba66fb6d-31cf-4ab9-a308-a4d8ec70595b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The roughly 140 hours of security camera video only compounds concerns over fairness in Lewiston's elections, revealing that more than 200 apparently non-English-speaking Somalis voted with the assistance -- or coaching -- of the handful of Somali NGO staffers who were stationed throughout City Hall for almost the entire early voting period.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1d3cf0a0-c577-4398-a81c-6b056fe70ed5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
On Oct. 20, Fetherston said he had seen translators "talking to people and pointing at the ballots," and "a couple of people actually touching the ballots."
In another segment, a woman with a backpack appears to point to items on a voter's ballot while a second translator walks over and watches. Multiple other segments show the NGO staffers manipulating and even filling out ballots -- a clear violation of state law.
Two Republican candidates for local office in Lewiston, who've both been observing the election at City Hall, have also observed troubling signs that the election in Lewiston isn't on the level.
Janet Beaudoin, the Republican running against Democratic Rep. Scott Harriman in House District 94, [told the City Council](https://substack.com/redirect/be689e91-3710-4fa6-a58e-6d2be93105f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that an interpreter said he'd tell the person he was helping to vote for her if she were a Democrat.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack.com/redirect/3ea55dc9-2438-433d-8ba7-260f44625703?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Lewiston City Councilor Bret Martel, the Republican running in House District 95, told MWTV that 12 to 20 people came into that hallway holding issue signs. He said complaints had already forced him to remove a plain paper name tag and to pull the campaign magnets off his truck.
Fetherston said [three complaints have been filed](https://substack.com/redirect/9f1a7fd2-25f4-4536-8935-bc048e5647f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with Lewiston police over the MPA's activity at City Hall and the conduct of translators.
A warden later told one interpreter to leave the voting area after the interpreter approached a newly arrived voter who hadn't asked for help, according to [City Clerk Kathy Montejo's account to Fetherston](https://substack.com/redirect/2f932878-5c37-470a-ac80-390fb76b1a3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
In response to the journalistic exposure of voting irregularities, the left-wing Maine People's Alliance staged a demonstration at City Hall -- a militant march through the institution which also appears to have violated Maine's statutes.
Maine law prohibits electioneering within 250 feet of the entrance to any polling place, and the MPA staffers can be seen on video marauding through City Hall with political signs. Those engaged in illicit electioneering include Democratic State Rep. Scott Harriman, who is also a candidate on the ballot in Lewiston.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/de53d55b-714d-49ee-807f-bcb2343616ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
One sign read "I am voting for my immigrant neighbors." The sign Harriman appears to hold read "I am voting for my community."
Secretary of State Shenna Bellows (D) said her office received complaints of "intrusive filming, photography and harassment of voters," and has said on privately recorded Zoom calls with left-wing activists that her office is investigating _The Maine Wire_.
With Election Day next Tuesday, the Maine GOP and Republican National Committee response to a brazen display of potentially illegal electioneering has been anemic. While the RNC has claimed to have observers on the ground in Lewiston, none have been seen. Meanwhile, the Maine GOP has sent four press releases this week with identical headlines touting party Chairman Jim Deyermond's recitation of Republican talking points regarding Troy Jackson.
On the other side of the aisle, Maine Democrats have held the governorship and both houses of the Legislature for nearly eight years. Yet despite the benefits of incumbency, they have grown increasingly bellicose in their bid to cling to power in Augusta.

In June 2023, then-House Speaker Rachel Talbot Ross (D), a business partner to Somali State Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D), told a Juneteenth event, "We should be storming the capitol," adding, "really, I'm serious."
The national reckoning over welfare fraud has, in Maine, centered on Lewiston and on one Somali-owned migrant agency with deep connections not only to the Maine Democratic Party but also to the very NGO staffers seen in the CCTV video hustling voters in and out of City Hall.
Following investigative reports from _The Robinson Report_ detailing welfare fraud allegations against the $5 million-per-year Gateway Community Services and its founder, Somali-American refugee Abdullahi Ali, Maine DHHS cut off MaineCare payments to the agency last December.
Although Gateway is now defunct, and Ali is on the lam in Africa, multiple former Gateway staffers continue to operate the political committee Ali and Gateway staffers formed after receiving lucrative no-bid contracts from the Mills Administration.
Those former Gateway staffers include Safiya Khalid, the director of the Community Organizing Alliance, who can be seen in CCTV footage orchestrating the movements of translators and voters, as well as Ahmed Aska Daher, a community health worker for Gateway.
How much of an influence could the Somali diaspora vote have in Lewiston, the Second Congressional District race, or even the U.S. Senate contest between Sen. Susan Collins and Graham Platner's replacement, Democrat Troy Jackson?
To estimate the total diaspora population voting in recent years, _The Robinson Report_ compared Maine's central voter registration data and other commercial data sets to a list of the 50,000 most common Somali names, which found an estimated 4,000 presumable Somalis registered to vote statewide, with approximately 1,300 of those voters providing addresses in Lewiston.
To vote legally in Maine, a person must be a U.S. citizen. For the voters in the video who were not born in the U.S. to be voting legally, they would need to be naturalized citizens. The presence of translators for hundreds of Somali voters raises the question as to how these individuals could be naturalized U.S. citizens if they don't speak English.
One possible explanation is that they are not, in fact, U.S. citizens, given Maine [Secretary of State Shenna Bellows' on-camera admission](https://substack.com/redirect/9bfcc6f8-88f8-4820-859e-5d3ce6c1736d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that she's aware that noncitizens are registered to vote in Maine.
However, there's another alternative. While naturalization normally requires an English test, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) lists a few exceptions. Under the 50/20 exception, an applicant who is 50 or older at the time of filing and has been a green card holder for 20 years is exempt from the English requirement.
Under 55/15, an applicant who is 55 or older and has been a green card holder for 15 years is exempt from the English requirement. Applicants who qualify for 50/20 or 55/15 still must take the civics test, but may take it in their native language with an interpreter they bring to the interview.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..JWtBhCfnq0WGlv4TnaAgPf4dHp2WndNOpUN4f7cV4wQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=222713896)
Under 65/20, an applicant who is 65 or older with 20 years as a permanent resident gets "special consideration regarding the civics requirement."
With Form N-648, an applicant who can't meet the English and civics requirements "because of a physical or developmental disability or a mental impairment" can request a medical exception. A licensed medical or osteopathic doctor or a licensed clinical psychologist must complete the form.
A voter who naturalized under one of those exceptions may be a citizen and still be unable to read an English ballot. Under section 672, that voter may ask for an aide.
So the more than 200 illiterate Somali voters seen on CCTV casting ballots with the help of one or more NGO staffers could well be naturalized U.S. citizens provided they applied for naturalization and were approved for one of those exceptions. According to USCIS data, the federal government hands out anywhere from 150,000-200,000 English proficiency exemptions in a given year.
In Maine, the rate of naturalizations has been modest: roughly 900-1,400 per year in recent years, according to the [Office of Homeland Security Statistics](https://substack.com/redirect/68ae8ea1-1ada-47d6-a356-7e64c40cb9cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Maine might be the only state where the Democrat Secretary of State openly admits that there are noncitizens registered to vote -- and then refuses to turn over voter records to the Department of Justice -- but it's not the only state where noncitizens on the ballot have become a political fight.
On Oct. 26, the Justice Department announced charges against 48 aliens in Pennsylvania, California, Florida, New York and Nevada for illegal voting, fraudulent registration and related crimes.
On Oct. 16, the department announced charges against 16 more in North Carolina, New York and Idaho. On Oct. 29, it announced 18 more indictments in North Carolina, bringing that state's total to 30 charged this year.
On Sept. 30, the department announced that a federal grand jury in Minnesota had indicted 10 foreign nationals, one of whom allegedly voted in this August's primary.
No charges have been filed in Maine related to noncitizens registering to vote or voting.

Lewiston City Councilor Bret Martel, the Republican running in House District 95, told MWTV that 12 to 20 people came into that hallway holding issue signs. He said complaints had already forced him to remove a plain paper name tag and to pull the campaign magnets off his truck. Fetherston said with Lewiston police over the MPA's activity at City Hall and the conduct of translators. A warden later told one interpreter to leave the voting area after the interpreter approached a newly arrived voter who hadn't asked for help, according to . In response to the journalistic exposure of voting irregularities, the left-wing Maine People's Alliance staged a demonstration at City Hall -- a militant march through the institution which also appears to have violated Maine's statutes. Maine law prohibits electioneering within 250 feet of the entrance to any polling place, and the MPA staffers can be seen on video marauding through City Hall with political signs. Those engaged in illicit electioneering include Democratic State Rep. Scott Harriman, who is also a candidate on the ballot in Lewiston. One sign read "I am voting for my immigrant neighbors." The sign Harriman appears to hold read "I am voting for my community." Secretary of State Shenna Bellows (D) said her office received complaints of "intrusive filming, photography and harassment of voters," and has said on privately recorded Zoom calls with left-wing activists that her office is investigating The Maine Wire. With Election Day next Tuesday, the Maine GOP and Republican National Committee response to a brazen display of potentially illegal electioneering has been anemic. While the RNC has claimed to have observers on the ground in Lewiston, none have been seen. Meanwhile, the Maine GOP has sent four press releases this week with identical headlines touting party Chairman Jim Deyermond's recitation of Republican talking points regarding Troy Jackson. On the other side of the aisle, Maine Democrats have held the governorship and both houses of the Legislature for nearly eight years. Yet despite the benefits of incumbency, they have grown increasingly bellicose in their bid to cling to power in Augusta. Want to help The Robinson Report? Share this post on Facebook and send it to your friends! In June 2023, then-House Speaker Rachel Talbot Ross (D), a business partner to Somali State Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D), told a Juneteenth event, "We should be storming the capitol," adding, "really, I'm serious." The national reckoning over welfare fraud has, in Maine, centered on Lewiston and on one Somali-owned migrant agency with deep connections not only to the Maine Democratic Party but also to the very NGO staffers seen in the CCTV video hustling voters in and out of City Hall. Following investigative reports from The Robinson Report detailing welfare fraud allegations against the $5 million-per-year Gateway Community Services and its founder, Somali-American refugee Abdullahi Ali, Maine DHHS cut off MaineCare payments to the agency last December. Although Gateway is now defunct, and Ali is on the lam in Africa, multiple former Gateway staffers continue to operate the political committee Ali and Gateway staffers formed after receiving lucrative no-bid contracts from the Mills Administration. Those former Gateway staffers include Safiya Khalid, the director of the Community Organizing Alliance, who can be seen in CCTV footage orchestrating the movements of translators and voters, as well as Ahmed Aska Daher, a community health worker for Gateway. How much of an influence could the Somali diaspora vote have in Lewiston, the Second Congressional District race, or even the U.S. Senate contest between Sen. Susan Collins and Graham Platner's replacement, Democrat Troy Jackson? To estimate the total diaspora population voting in recent years, The Robinson Report compared Maine's central voter registration data and other commercial data sets to a list of the 50,000 most common Somali names, which found an estimated 4,000 presumable Somalis registered to vote statewide, with approximately 1,300 of those voters providing addresses in Lewiston. To vote legally in Maine, a person must be a U.S. citizen. For the voters in the video who were not born in the U.S. to be voting legally, they would need to be naturalized citizens. The presence of translators for hundreds of Somali voters raises the question as to how these individuals could be naturalized U.S. citizens if they don't speak English. One possible explanation is that they are not, in fact, U.S. citizens, given Maine that she's aware that noncitizens are registered to vote in Maine. However, there's another alternative. While naturalization normally requires an English test, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) lists a few exceptions. Under the 50/20 exception, an applicant who is 50 or older at the time of filing and has been a green card holder for 20 years is exempt from the English requirement. Under 55/15, an applicant who is 55 or older and has been a green card holder for 15 years is exempt from the English requirement. Applicants who qualify for 50/20 or 55/15 still must take the civics test, but may take it in their native language with an interpreter they bring to the interview. Under 65/20, an applicant who is 65 or older with 20 years as a permanent resident gets "special consideration regarding the civics requirement." With Form N-648, an applicant who can't meet the English and civics requirements "because of a physical or developmental disability or a mental impairment" can request a medical exception. A licensed medical or osteopathic doctor or a licensed clinical psychologist must complete the form. A voter who naturalized under one of those exceptions may be a citizen and still be unable to read an English ballot. Under section 672, that voter may ask for an aide. So the more than 200 illiterate Somali voters seen on CCTV casting ballots with the help of one or more NGO staffers could well be naturalized U.S. citizens provided they applied for naturalization and were approved for one of those exceptions. According to USCIS data, the federal government hands out anywhere from 150,000-200,000 English proficiency exemptions in a given year. In Maine, the rate of naturalizations has been modest: roughly 900-1,400 per year in recent years, according to the . Maine might be the only state where the Democrat Secretary of State openly admits that there are noncitizens registered to vote -- and then refuses to turn over voter records to the Department of Justice -- but it's not the only state where noncitizens on the ballot have become a political fight. On Oct. 26, the Justice Department announced charges against 48 aliens in Pennsylvania, California, Florida, New York and Nevada for illegal voting, fraudulent registration and related crimes. On Oct. 16, the department announced charges against 16 more in North Carolina, New York and Idaho. On Oct. 29, it announced 18 more indictments in North Carolina, bringing that state's total to 30 charged this year. On Sept. 30, the department announced that a federal grand jury in Minnesota had indicted 10 foreign nationals, one of whom allegedly voted in this August's primary. * Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/26c05e16-8956-4ae8-8b0d-961c81f24271?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X that Tehran's conditions had been "repeatedly and clearly stated to the mediators," adding that "the carrot-and-stick approach has no effect on Iran," and that progress was possible only once Iran's proposals were accepted.

* **NYT: U.S. oil companies take $130+ billion in recent profits during Iran war, Americans pay $147 billion for fuel:** More than 50 major U.S. oil and gas companies [earned](https://substack.com/redirect/01e8f879-87e5-42d8-861b-432ccfd9ce1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over $130 billion in profits between April and September during the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, according to a New York Times analysis. * **Vance insists Trump will not let Iran conflict become a "forever war": **U.S. Vice President JD Vance [defended](https://substack.com/redirect/d90c72fa-9376-4026-b7e6-1014923444f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Trump administration's military campaign against Iran during a Fox News town hall in Fort Worth, Texas, after a Republican voter questioned whether the administration had fulfilled its promise to end costly foreign wars.

* **U.S. demands Iran cooperate with IAEA despite military attacks that halted inspections:** U.S. Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz accused Iran of failing to cooperate with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) at a UN Security Council meeting, telling Tehran's delegation, "Your lies are no good here," and insisting that the nuclear watchdog needed "answers, not speeches."

* Grossi said that Tehran had previously agreed to allow inspectors into its Isfahan enrichment facility, however, "the commencement of the attacks prevented our inspector from going to the site."
* He added that the agency had identified no repairs or reconstruction at nuclear facilities damaged in the 2025 and 2026 attacks.
* **Small boat attaches explosives to tanker in Strait of Hormuz, sparking engine-room fire:** A tanker was attacked with explosive devices in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, approximately 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).

* UKMTO said that the crew extinguished the fire and resumed its journey, with no injuries or environmental damage reported.
* Separately, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said it had stopped two oil tankers in the southern waters of the strait after they allegedly switched off their navigation systems and attempted to travel through unauthorized routes with U.S. military support. * **Dockworkers at 110 ports across 22 countries strike against wars on Gaza and Iran:** Dockworkers at more than 110 ports across 22 countries on five continents are [striking](https://substack.com/redirect/01542563-7a24-4f66-aad5-f103523b042f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Friday, under the slogan "Dockworkers do not work for war," demanding an end to Israel's genocide in Gaza and U.S.-Israeli military attacks on Iran and expressing solidarity with Cuba, Venezuela, and Sudan.

* **Netanyahu loses majority in Israeli election, rules out coalition with Arab-led parties:** Israel's Central Elections Committee [published](https://substack.com/redirect/d5f70b39-dd20-4170-a1b5-d7ef76dc8b2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the final results of Tuesday's election early Friday. A sixth operation targeted Saudi military forces in Najran.
* Saudi-led forces said they intercepted and destroyed a drone over the Islamic holy city of Mecca on Friday, according to Saudi-coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki, attributing the drone to Ansarallah. * **Saudi strikes kill 27 in Yemen:** Saudi airstrikes on Yemen's Taiz province [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/b31d2127-392b-450c-adf3-2891a559ee60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least 13 people on Thursday, most of them women and children, according to the Health Ministry in Sana'a. Alaska Gov. **Mike Dunleavy** ordered a state investigation into the matter. * **DOJ says FBI and ICE personnel won 't serve as midterm poll monitors, but other federal agents will:** The DOJ [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3a2d6326-1fa9-4b2b-9926-f94e1a72134d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a court filing on Wednesday that ICE and FBI employees will not monitor the midterm elections next week. Instead, agents of the Bureau of Prisons, the ATF, and the DEA will. The disclosure follows a suit from the NAACP that sought to bar prosecutors and law enforcement from monitoring polling places. The DOJ said that agents of the Bureau of Prisons, the ATF, and the DEA will stand outside the polls to observe the scene, take notes, and interview willing voters. The federal agents will not act as law enforcement officials, the DOJ added, and will not carry firearms. DHS Secretary **Markwayne Mullin** said in September that ICE would not patrol or monitor polling sites but could be present "if there is a threat to that polling place or we're serving a warrant on someone that we have been actively tracking down."
