name: The Turning Point Action Team
subject: Here's what's really on the line...
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TURNING POINT ACTION (TPACTION
body:
Three states are about to decide a lot more than 2026.

| | | |
---
Peter,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let us explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

If the Academy were handing out awards for political performances, Congressman Jim Himes might have earned an Emmy nomination for last night's debate.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..MpA7dR4AsF-tUFLOH43UwYLFfk6xhoK9lsqCLiB9Dds?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=222492135)

**And the award for Best Performance in a Political Fiction goes to ... Hollywood Jim!**
At the October 29 congressional debate hosted by CT Examiner at Stamford's Ferguson Library, Himes returned to a familiar theme: Donald Trump.
When I checked the online recording, it had just 129 views. The audience appeared to include plenty of Himes supporters and campaign volunteers.
But the familiar performance continued and my response was simple:
**" This debate is between me and Jim Himes. Donald Trump is not here this evening, and he probably does not even know who I am."**
I came to discuss Connecticut's future and the record of a congressman who has represented this district since 2009.
Our families are dealing with expensive healthcare, high electricity bills, congested highways and limited opportunities for young people.
We have two Democratic U.S. senators, five Democratic members of Congress, a Democratic governor and Democratic control of both chambers of the state legislature.
That concentration of power deserves scrutiny.
**At what point do we stop blaming the opposition and start examining the record of those already in office?**
[Watch the October 29 debate on CT-N](https://substack.com/redirect/69c2b0d0-7269-4555-a8f1-6bffa76c4c81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## The Surprise: Hollywood Jim Agreed With Me
Perhaps the most revealing part of the evening was how often Himes and I found common ground.
He acknowledged problems with excessive regulation and the Washington bureaucracy. I pointed out that the Republican Party is the party of smaller government. We discussed nuclear energy, protecting Long Island Sound, and aspects of gender-affirming healthcare where our positions were closer than many might expect.
I welcomed those agreements, but they also raised an obvious question:
**If Jim recognizes these problems, what has he accomplished toward solving them after nearly 18 years?**
Agreement at a debate is valuable. Results matter more.
## Transit-Oriented Development: What About the Sewage?
Himes promoted transit-oriented development and affordable housing.
I recognize the benefits of housing near transportation. It can improve access to jobs and reduce automobile dependence.
But I asked a question too often overlooked:
**Where is all the sewage going to go?**
Every new apartment adds demand to water, wastewater and other infrastructure.
More housing near train stations may reduce traffic. It doesn't eliminate toilets, showers or sewage.
Long Island Sound communities already confront bacterial contamination, wastewater overflows and beach closures.
Connecticut DEEP identifies heavy rainfall, insufficient sewer capacity and aging infrastructure among the causes of untreated sewage discharges.
We should evaluate sewer capacity during major storms, not simply under normal dry-weather conditions.
I support affordable housing, but development and environmental protection must proceed together.
**You cannot call development progress if the beaches downstream become unusable.**
[Connecticut DEEP: Sewage Right-to-Know](https://substack.com/redirect/b20ed07a-d1e7-4670-a4a2-11301c5880a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Connecticut DEEP: Current and Historical Sewage Overflow Data](https://substack.com/redirect/d7b3dea3-6238-4183-8e69-71451e27e231?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## Social Security: 5.6% or 2.6%?
One of our most important exchanges concerned Social Security's financial future.
Himes cited an interest rate of approximately 5.6%, as I understood him.
But the Social Security Administration's 2026 Trustees Report shows that the combined trust funds earned an effective annual interest rate of **2.6% in 2025**. Newly issued special Treasury securities averaged 4.3%. The Trust Fund needs a higher return on their investment to keep Social Security solvent.
The combined trust funds are projected to exhaust their reserves in 2034 under current-law assumptions.
I believe Congress should examine whether a carefully limited portion of Social Security reserves could be invested in diversified, low-cost equity index funds, including funds tracking the S&P 500, rather than relying exclusively on Treasury securities.
Equities have historically delivered higher long-term returns, but they also involve real market risk. Any reform would require independent management, liquidity protections and strict safeguards for beneficiaries.
I am not suggesting we gamble retirees' benefits. Yet all pension funds invest in the market. Pension funds tend to be conservative investors.
I believe the system can responsibly pursue better long-term returns, as other pension plans do.
**Social Security deserves accurate numbers and a serious discussion of its financial future.**
[Social Security Administration: 2026 Trustees Report](https://substack.com/redirect/ec3f95c1-137b-40ec-ab21-3fca360cf024?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Congressional Research Service: How Social Security Trust Funds Are Invested](https://substack.com/redirect/33580eb6-0119-49d1-b98d-ac5e692479c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## And Remember: Jim Is Coming for Your Inheritance
Although we didn't discuss inheritance at this debate, I haven't forgotten our earlier exchange at the [October 19 Westport Library debate](https://substack.com/redirect/d2665649-3155-4abe-bf9a-165fb9521e9b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Himes, a middle-class man with a net worth north of 13 million, described stocks inherited from his mother and discussed changing the tax treatment known as the _step-up in basis_.
That provision generally resets the tax basis of qualifying inherited assets to their fair market value at death.
Changing it could affect families inheriting investments, resal estate or family businesses, depending on how legislation is structured.
I support the right for heirs to inherit from their parents tax free up to the current limits. This should remain unchanged.
[IRS: Understanding the Basis of Inherited Property](https://substack.com/redirect/a77045f2-9349-4c51-bc8c-bd65ad7df67c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## Healthcare: I'm a Doctor. Jim Defends the System.
Healthcare is one of the reasons I entered this race. It is the number one affordability issue masked by the fear of high gas prices.
Himes supported the Affordable Care Act. That law expanded coverage and protections, but it has not resolved the affordability problems confronting many families. In fact healthcare costs have doubled since the passage of the ACA.
Patients still face expensive premiums, high deductibles and complicated insurance requirements. Preventive medicine is not emphasized.
As a physician, I want to focus on prevention, transparent pricing, competition, lower administrative costs and protection against catastrophic medical expenses.
Doctors should spend more time treating patients and less time fighting insurance companies over paperwork.
**Healthcare should be about patients, not paperwork.**
## Nuclear Power, I-95 and the Missing Bridge
Himes and I agreed that nuclear energy and fossil fuels should play a role in America's energy future.
But Connecticut also needs reliable natural gas supply and an energy policy that recognizes the costs faced by households and businesses.
On transportation, I raised the Congress Street Bridge in Bridgeport, which has remained out of service throughout Himes's congressional tenure.
I also questioned the continuing congestion on I-95 and the fact that our mail is sorted in White Plains and not Connecticut.
Himes cant point to federal infrastructure investments that he has made in CT. Those investments deserve consideration and now he support them - another area where we agree.
But voters should also examine the projects that remain unfinished. He has a record of empty promises, I have a record of taking action from the bleachers.
**You cannot drive across a press release.**
## Iran: Diplomacy or a Dangerous Cancer?
One of our strongest disagreements concerned Iran.
I described the Iranian regime's nuclear ambitions as a dangerous cancer that cannot be allowed to spread.
Himes emphasized diplomacy, inspections and his intelligence experience and access to classified information.
I recognize the importance of those tools. But inspections are not infallible, and agreements require effective verification and enforcement.
**The question isn 't simply whether another agreement can be negotiated. It's whether it can reliably prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.**
That is a substantive foreign-policy disagreement deserving serious debate.
## Gaza: Hamas, Public Opinion and Campaign Contributions
Himes and I agreed in condemning Hamas, but disagreed over the extent of its support in Gaza.
My questions about Hamas's continuing influence drew boos from parts of the audience.
I believe we must distinguish support for Hamas as a political organization from opposition to its disarmament and the real statistics on the "genocide".
The Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research's October 2026 poll reported substantial opposition to disarming Hamas before a complete Israeli withdrawal: **69% among Gaza respondents**.
That is not the same as majority support for Hamas as a political party, but it is relevant to discussions about demilitarization and future security and the challenges of peace in the region.
I believe both Israeli security and the protection of Palestinian civilians must be part of any durable peace. I also believe that when it comes to many middle eastern conflicts, we cannot impose western solutions.
There is another point worth considering.
According to Track AIPAC, Himes has received **$76,408 in contributions associated with pro-Israel PACs over his federal career** , as classified by that organization.
That is a career total, not a verified figure for this election cycle. I have no AIPAC support despite a Jewish last name.
Receiving contributions from domestic political committees does not establish someone's motives or loyalty. But public campaign-finance records deserve transparency.
**We should debate policy and evidence without questioning one another 's patriotism.**
[Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research: October 2026 Poll](https://substack.com/redirect/be3cf392-2ba2-4bf6-9855-b4b6b20c993d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Track AIPAC: Connecticut Congressional Contributions](https://substack.com/redirect/0b3e1e5c-b0b6-4ca8-9be1-2ac2d2c38e31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## The Political Left and Social Issues
I also challenged Himes about the influence of the Democratic Party's socialist wing, including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Abdul El-Sayed.
Himes characterized that influence as relatively limited.
I believe even small factions can shape legislative priorities, and voters deserve to understand how their representatives would respond to their proposals.
_**On gender-affirming healthcare, we found areas of common ground.**_
Himes also focused on abortion restrictions in Florida and other states. Those issues matter in federal policy, but Connecticut already has broad abortion protections.
The important question is what each candidate actually proposes for Congress.
These discussions deserve greater nuance than campaign advertising usually provides. There are also emotional responses where I may come at this from a physician's perspective.
## The Final Act: Results, Not Another Performance
Jim Himes is an experienced politician with weekly sound bytes. His supporters can point to legislation, federal investments and positions they consider accomplishments that have not improved outcomes.
I disagree with much of his record and believe major problems remain inadequately addressed.
_**One area we did not discuss was Himes ' record voting against a bill that would deport illegals that commit violent crimes against Women and Children - If he had supported it maybe Liam Rivera, an innocent 2 year old would still be alive.**_
Yet, last night's debate demonstrated something important: We could identify shared concerns about regulation, nuclear energy, clean water and the cost of living, even while disagreeing about the solutions.
We also debated substantial differences on Healthcare, Social Security, Iran and Hamas.
These are the discussions a congressional race should encourage and it is fascinating how much Himes agrees with me. He went in 18 years ago to be moderate and cross political lines - He has failed at that. He votes 95% of the time with the Democrat Party. With my experience, I know I can and I will not be a puppet or rubberstamp to the President who does not know my name or seem to care about putting any attention to the people of Fairfield County.
_**Instead, we repeatedly returned to Donald Trump.**_
I am not Donald Trump.
I am a doctor, an attorney and a Connecticut resident who believes our congressional race should focus on Connecticut's families and our future, not an audition for Hollywood squares.
**After nearly 18 years, Himes should be judged not only by the dangers he warns about, but by the problems he has helped solve and those he has not solved.**
Connecticut's challenges are not a television production.
They require good policy, serious analysis and accountable representation.
**Give Hollywood Jim an Emmy for the performance.**
**Then let 's get back to discussing Connecticut's future and saving the state.**
* * *
_Dr. Michael Goldstein is a physician, attorney and Republican candidate for Congress in Connecticut 's Fourth Congressional District._

And the award for Best Performance in a Political Fiction goes to ... Hollywood Jim! At the October 29 congressional debate hosted by CT Examiner at Stamford's Ferguson Library, Himes returned to a familiar theme: Donald Trump. When I checked the online recording, it had just 129 views. The audience appeared to include plenty of Himes supporters and campaign volunteers. But the familiar performance continued and my response was simple: " This debate is between me and Jim Himes. Donald Trump is not here this evening, and he probably does not even know who I am." I came to discuss Connecticut's future and the record of a congressman who has represented this district since 2009. Our families are dealing with expensive healthcare, high electricity bills, congested highways and limited opportunities for young people. We have two Democratic U.S. senators, five Democratic members of Congress, a Democratic governor and Democratic control of both chambers of the state legislature. That concentration of power deserves scrutiny. At what point do we stop blaming the opposition and start examining the record of those already in office? The Surprise: Hollywood Jim Agreed With Me Perhaps the most revealing part of the evening was how often Himes and I found common ground. He acknowledged problems with excessive regulation and the Washington bureaucracy. I pointed out that the Republican Party is the party of smaller government. We discussed nuclear energy, protecting Long Island Sound, and aspects of gender-affirming healthcare where our positions were closer than many might expect. I welcomed those agreements, but they also raised an obvious question: If Jim recognizes these problems, what has he accomplished toward solving them after nearly 18 years? Agreement at a debate is valuable. Results matter more. Transit-Oriented Development: What About the Sewage? Himes promoted transit-oriented development and affordable housing. I recognize the benefits of housing near transportation. It can improve access to jobs and reduce automobile dependence. But I asked a question too often overlooked: Where is all the sewage going to go? Every new apartment adds demand to water, wastewater and other infrastructure. More housing near train stations may reduce traffic. It doesn't eliminate toilets, showers or sewage. Long Island Sound communities already confront bacterial contamination, wastewater overflows and beach closures. Connecticut DEEP identifies heavy rainfall, insufficient sewer capacity and aging infrastructure among the causes of untreated sewage discharges. We should evaluate sewer capacity during major storms, not simply under normal dry-weather conditions. I support affordable housing, but development and environmental protection must proceed together. You cannot call development progress if the beaches downstream become unusable. Social Security: 5.6% or 2.6%? One of our most important exchanges concerned Social Security's financial future. Himes cited an interest rate of approximately 5.6%, as I understood him. But the Social Security Administration's 2026 Trustees Report shows that the combined trust funds earned an effective annual interest rate of 2.6% in 2025. Newly issued special Treasury securities averaged 4.3%. The Trust Fund needs a higher return on their investment to keep Social Security solvent. The combined trust funds are projected to exhaust their reserves in 2034 under current-law assumptions. I believe Congress should examine whether a carefully limited portion of Social Security reserves could be invested in diversified, low-cost equity index funds, including funds tracking the S&P 500, rather than relying exclusively on Treasury securities. Equities have historically delivered higher long-term returns, but they also involve real market risk. Any reform would require independent management, liquidity protections and strict safeguards for beneficiaries. I am not suggesting we gamble retirees' benefits. Yet all pension funds invest in the market. Pension funds tend to be conservative investors. I believe the system can responsibly pursue better long-term returns, as other pension plans do. Social Security deserves accurate numbers and a serious discussion of its financial future. And Remember: Jim Is Coming for Your Inheritance Although we didn't discuss inheritance at this debate, I haven't forgotten our earlier exchange at the . Himes, a middle-class man with a net worth north of 13 million, described stocks inherited from his mother and discussed changing the tax treatment known as the step-up in basis. That provision generally resets the tax basis of qualifying inherited assets to their fair market value at death. Changing it could affect families inheriting investments, resal estate or family businesses, depending on how legislation is structured. I support the right for heirs to inherit from their parents tax free up to the current limits. This should remain unchanged. Healthcare: I'm a Doctor. Jim Defends the System. Healthcare is one of the reasons I entered this race. It is the number one affordability issue masked by the fear of high gas prices. Himes supported the Affordable Care Act. That law expanded coverage and protections, but it has not resolved the affordability problems confronting many families. In fact healthcare costs have doubled since the passage of the ACA. Patients still face expensive premiums, high deductibles and complicated insurance requirements. Preventive medicine is not emphasized. As a physician, I want to focus on prevention, transparent pricing, competition, lower administrative costs and protection against catastrophic medical expenses. Doctors should spend more time treating patients and less time fighting insurance companies over paperwork. Healthcare should be about patients, not paperwork. Nuclear Power, I-95 and the Missing Bridge Himes and I agreed that nuclear energy and fossil fuels should play a role in America's energy future. But Connecticut also needs reliable natural gas supply and an energy policy that recognizes the costs faced by households and businesses. On transportation, I raised the Congress Street Bridge in Bridgeport, which has remained out of service throughout Himes's congressional tenure. I also questioned the continuing congestion on I-95 and the fact that our mail is sorted in White Plains and not Connecticut. Himes cant point to federal infrastructure investments that he has made in CT. Those investments deserve consideration and now he support them - another area where we agree. But voters should also examine the projects that remain unfinished. He has a record of empty promises, I have a record of taking action from the bleachers. You cannot drive across a press release. Iran: Diplomacy or a Dangerous Cancer? One of our strongest disagreements concerned Iran. I described the Iranian regime's nuclear ambitions as a dangerous cancer that cannot be allowed to spread. Himes emphasized diplomacy, inspections and his intelligence experience and access to classified information. I recognize the importance of those tools. But inspections are not infallible, and agreements require effective verification and enforcement. The question isn 't simply whether another agreement can be negotiated. It's whether it can reliably prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. That is a substantive foreign-policy disagreement deserving serious debate. My questions about Hamas's continuing influence drew boos from parts of the audience. I believe we must distinguish support for Hamas as a political organization from opposition to its disarmament and the real statistics on the "genocide". I believe both Israeli security and the protection of Palestinian civilians must be part of any durable peace. clean_body: Beth, is this really as close as they say? | | Peter, Everywhere I go in these final days, people ask me the same question. Beth, is this really as close as they say? Here is my honest answer. Yes. It is that close, and it is that serious. The House majority could come down to a handful of seats, the forecasters have Democrats favored to take it, and the left has made North Texas a target. A race like this is decided in the final days by one thing: who fights hardest to the very end. And I am asking you to fight it with me. | | Four days. We win this by refusing to let up. Thank you for being in it. Beth Van Duyne | PAID FOR BY BETH VAN DUYNE FOR CONGRESS

In February, Investors Dumped Nearly $1 Trillion of Software Stocks in Days. They Were Betting on Which Companies AI Will Hurt.
The selloff started when new AI tools showed they could do work that companies pay software firms to handle. Goldman Sachs soon launched a basket of stocks it expects to win or lose from AI. Yesterday, early voting opened in Kentucky. I couldn't be prouder to cast my vote alongside my family.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49d2f296-3716-444b-b6b3-ea251e1e33c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

You might think that now that votes are being cast, we're slowing down our efforts and accepting whatever happens next.
But this race is far from over. Over the next four days, we're going to meet _THOUSANDS_ of Kentuckians and mobilize them to the polls.
This race will be won or lost this weekend. After millions of dollars from Andy Barr's super PAC allies, our polling has my MAGA opponent and I tied. That means **your donation from this point on can make or break this campaign in the most pivotal moment.**
Boots on the ground campaigning like this is expensive. You've been so generous with your time and donations thus far. We wouldn't keep asking you to chip in if the stakes weren't as high as they are.
Please, step up and chip in to help us reach my final end-of-month goal before Election Day.
[Chip in to my Senate Campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/49d2f296-3716-444b-b6b3-ea251e1e33c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Your generosity doesn't go unnoticed. Thank you for putting your faith in me.
_Charles Booker_

One
sentence. That’s all it took for the Supreme Court to wipe out a due
process protection immigrants have relied on.

And not a single Justice signed the order. Here’s what they took away:

For years, an immigration judge could put a deportation case on hold while
a person’s other legal fights played out, like a request for humanitarian
relief or a separate path to legal status. Judges have used this power
360,000 times in more than three decades.^1

And when these cases get reopened, the majority of them get to keep their
place in this country. So of course Trump wanted it gone, and it was
disturbingly simple.

In 2024, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton sued to kill the Biden rule
protecting this power.

This year, Trump’s DOJ, which should have defended the rule, joined Texas
in court instead and asked the judge to scrap it. The judge went along
with it.

Three cities called the deal “egregious collusion” and asked the Supreme
Court to step in. The Roberts Court shrugged. One unsigned order, and the
whole scheme stands.

Now judges have lost the power to slow down Trump’s deportation machine. A
survivor waiting on protection. A child waiting to tell their story. Their
futures can be shoved toward deportation before their claims are ever
heard.

We cannot let this go. Demand Justice PAC is exposing this Court, holding
every politician who enables it accountable, and building the pressure for
an independent Court that protects the people, not a wannabe
authoritarian.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1005&refcode=20261030_Brazil_T1&akid=295%2E344797%2EEQeTYS ]COURIER Newsroom

Peter,

Last weekend, Brazilian voters narrowly re-elected President Lula da
Silva. But according to reporting by Al Jazeera and others, they had to
overcome interference by Big Tech every step of the way:

* Watchdogs collected 1,100 reports of accounts being removed or
throttled on Meta’s platforms, mostly accounts supporting Lula.
* Lula’s own ad account was briefly suspended.
* In a test, Meta approved 13 of 15 ads containing AI-generated violence
and disinformation.

(Meta denies favoring any candidate.)

Just days away from our own Election Day, the lesson is clear. A handful
of billionaires may own the platforms where most voters get their news.
But we refuse to hand those feeds over to them.

With local newsrooms in 20 states, COURIER reaches millions of people
every day with independent, factual news and analysis, right in the feeds
and inboxes where they already are. If we’re not there, disinformation
fills the space.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11540?t=1003&refcode=20261030_Brazil_T1&akid=295%2E344797%2EEQeTYS ]Can you contribute $25 to help COURIER keep the truth in front of
voters through Election Day and beyond?

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/11540?t=1004&refcode=20261030_Brazil_T1&akid=295%2E344797%2EEQeTYS ]Contribute $25

We may not be able to change who owns the platforms or how they engineer
their algorithms, but we can change what’s on them.

Thanks for standing with us,

The COURIER Team

Hi Peter – it's Senator Adam Schiff. I’m reaching out today on behalf of my friend and colleague George Whitesides. clean_body: | = I was asked point-blank, friend: why should anyone send you back to Washington? My work’s not done. Despite serving in the minority during my first term, I brought $14 million back to the cities I represent. That’s our tax dollars being reinvested here at home, and I fought tooth and claw for every dollar. But there’s a lot more I need to do. When the GKN plant emergency forced evacuations across our community, I pushed to get our first responders the resources they needed. Families and small businesses who were forced out still haven’t been made whole, and I’m going to keep pressing GKN until they are. = | = My opponent, Chuong Vo, is running on his law enforcement background. What he conveniently doesn’t mention is that law enforcement is backing me, including the LA and Orange County sheriffs’ unions and even the California Fraternal Order of Police. I’ll put my record up against his any day. Voting is underway across CA-45, and every day more voters lock in their choice. name: Angie Nixon
subject: Years in power. Look at the results.
body:
Peter, Angie
Nixon here.

Republicans have controlled Florida for years, and they cannot hold that
much power while pretending they bear no responsibility for what working
families are experiencing: grocery bills that keep climbing, rent and
insurance eating up paychecks, childcare families can't afford, and
healthcare that costs too much.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20261030-movement-split.Z1LtSS&refcode=em20261030-2880&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1001&akid=2880%2E342411%2E5Oejf1 ]Can you split $10 between the Squad Victory Fund and me right now, with
Election Day closing in, to help change that in November?

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20261030-movement-split.Z1LtSS&refcode=em20261030-2880&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=2880%2E342411%2E5Oejf1 ]CHIP IN $10

Here's what Republicans understand about me, and why it scares them. I
shocked the political establishment by winning the Democratic nomination
despite being dramatically outspent, proving that people-powered
organizing can beat big money.

I'm a working-class Black woman who isn't going to Washington to protect
wealthy donors or preserve the status quo. I've been clear about why I'm
running: I want government to work for working people instead of the
wealthy and powerful interests that have dominated Washington and
Tallahassee.

The wealthy and powerful keep getting richer while working people are told
to make do with less. This campaign exists to ask the question at the
center of this race: who is the government working for, the people working
to pay the bills, or the wealthy few writing the checks?

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20261030-movement-split.Z1LtSS&refcode=em20261030-2880&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1003&akid=2880%2E342411%2E5Oejf1 ]Can you split $10, $25, or whatever you can between the Squad Victory
Fund and me right now, with Election Day closing in, to help keep building
a campaign that answers to voters?

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20261030-movement-split.Z1LtSS&refcode=em20261030-2880&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1022&akid=2880%2E342411%2E5Oejf1 ]Contribute ››

Their track record got us here. Let's give Florida a different one.

In solidarity,

Angie Nixon
Democratic Nominee, Florida U.S. Senate

subject: Four Days Left: Let’s Finish Strong and Celebrate Together!
body:
Dear Peter, Thank you. Your support has helped build the momentum putting Molly in the lead ahead of Tuesday’s election. Vermonters are ready for a Lieutenant Governor who will lower costs, deliver affordable healthcare and housing, and protect fundamental rights. Now, **we’re just four days from Election Day, and we need all hands on deck to finish strong.** _**Here are four ways you can help Team Molly in the final FOUR days:**_ **1\. Join a phone bank.** Right now, calling voters is the single most important way you can help (and it’s fun!). Every conversation matters, and every vote counts. Tomorrow, we’re hosting a special **[HALLOWEEN PHONE BANK at 11 AM](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142560588/657307177/-748575199?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MDRmOWEzMy1hM2Q0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=HPjSkpCQ4P9rKmeLXEyrKiM7hyMknbDTfvdJo7Mok-Y=&emci=57010dea-a1d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=604f9a33-a3d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=43402276)** , and we hope you’ll join us at our Burlington office or virtually in costume! No experience necessary: every shift starts with a quick training on our easy-to-use software and ends with a debrief. Join us to get out the vote for Molly in this final stretch: [https://www.mobilize.us/mollygrayforvermont/](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142560589/657307178/-188935202?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MDRmOWEzMy1hM2Q0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=HPjSkpCQ4P9rKmeLXEyrKiM7hyMknbDTfvdJo7Mok-Y=&emci=57010dea-a1d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=604f9a33-a3d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=43402276) **2\. Stand at the polls.** Help us show up strong on Election Day! **[Sign up HERE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142560590/657307179/-544431020?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MDRmOWEzMy1hM2Q0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=HPjSkpCQ4P9rKmeLXEyrKiM7hyMknbDTfvdJo7Mok-Y=&emci=57010dea-a1d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=604f9a33-a3d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=43402276)** to let us know you'd like to represent Team Molly at your local polling place. We'll provide everything you need to energize and inform voters. **3\. Make sure your family and friends vote.** This election will come down to who shows up. Take a few minutes to check in with your family, friends, neighbors, and coworkers. Make sure they have a plan to vote on or before November 3, and encourage them to support Molly! Have questions about voting? Visit the **[Secretary of State's voter guide](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142560591/657307180/1509533962?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MDRmOWEzMy1hM2Q0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=HPjSkpCQ4P9rKmeLXEyrKiM7hyMknbDTfvdJo7Mok-Y=&emci=57010dea-a1d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=604f9a33-a3d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=43402276)** or reach out to us. We're happy to help. **4\. Spread the word on social media.** Have you voted for Molly? Let people know! Share why you're supporting Molly on Facebook, Instagram, X, or TikTok, and tag our campaign. More than ever, people turn to friends, family, and neighbors they trust when deciding how to vote. Your voice can make a real difference. **And then, let's celebrate together on Election Night!** After months of phone calls, community conversations, and hard work, we want to celebrate with YOU. Join Team Molly and Democrats up and down the ballot next Tuesday at the Vermont Democratic Party's **Election Night Watch Party at Burlington City Arts!** We'll gather to watch the results roll in, celebrate everything we've accomplished together, and look ahead to what's next for Vermont. Expect a DJ, light food, a cash bar, and plenty of familiar faces. Bring your friends and family, and let's make it a night to remember! **WHEN** : Tuesday, November 3, at 6:45 PM **WHERE** : Burlington City Arts, 405 Pine Street, Burlington **[RSVP HERE!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142560592/657307181/913057118?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MDRmOWEzMy1hM2Q0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=HPjSkpCQ4P9rKmeLXEyrKiM7hyMknbDTfvdJo7Mok-Y=)** Space is limited, so don’t wait to RSVP! We're so close, but there's still work to do. Every call, every conversation, and every vote counts. **Let's finish strong, and then let's celebrate together.** With gratitude, _Team Molly_ | | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142560593/657307182/679520187?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MDRmOWEzMy1hM2Q0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=HPjSkpCQ4P9rKmeLXEyrKiM7hyMknbDTfvdJo7Mok-Y=)

body:
# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=1215%2E127862%2EzYRKR3)
Folks,
Election Day is this Tuesday, November 3rd — and we can’t win this toss-up race without your help!
This race will come down to the voters who still haven’t made up their minds. The best way to reach them is by canvassing and phone banking. _**That’s where you come in.**_
Team Ford is reaching undecided voters every single day between now and Election Day, and we need everybody on deck. [_**Can you sign up for a volunteer or phone bank shift?**_](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/239?t=3&akid=1215%2E127862%2EzYRKR3)
**[Volunteer With Us ››](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/239?t=4&akid=1215%2E127862%2EzYRKR3)**
Don’t worry, you don’t need to be a seasoned organizer to make an impact. You’ll be provided with everything you need to get started.
Whether you’re local or looking to help out from afar, there are opportunities for you.
[_**Help us make the most of the final get-out-the-vote weekend by signing up to volunteer today!**_](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/239?t=5&akid=1215%2E127862%2EzYRKR3)
Thanks for being part of this,
Team Ford
Make a plan to vote on or before November 3! [**Click here for resources ››**](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/225?t=6&akid=1215%2E127862%2EzYRKR3)

name: Sen. Jeff Bridges
subject: Mayor Pete's first campaign wasn't for president
body:
Pete Buttigieg told a packed room how hard it is to get people excited about a State Treasurer's race. He would know. He ran for Indiana Treasurer

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/0c158f08ae89/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10379908?e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/cszvp2keBj1?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,
On Wednesday in Highlands Ranch, Pete Buttigieg told a packed room how hard it is to get people excited about a State Treasurer's race. He would know. He ran for Indiana State Treasurer in 2010.
**I shouted back, "The most important office in the state!" Everyone laughed. I was only kind of joking.**
Congressman Joe Neguse, who grew up in Highlands Ranch, joined us alongside longtime Douglas County Democrats. Having grown up in Arapahoe County, I know what it’s like when red counties turn blue. This is their year.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1AXH8hm6I5V?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | Nobody talks about faith and governing better than Pete.
I've long believed a budget is a moral document. It puts in dollars and cents exactly what we value and how much. The same goes for our investments, because where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
**That's why the Treasurer's office matters. We can put Colorado dollars to work in Colorado to build homes people can afford, renewable energy that lowers bills, and child care that doesn't cost more than rent.**
Pete told me he appreciated how I explained why the Treasurer's office matters. He'd struggled with that when he ran. I told him things seem to have worked out pretty well for him all the same.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/E718RZ0ATZE?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | It's too late to mail your ballot! Use an official drop box or voting center by 7 p.m. Tuesday, November 3.
[Find your nearest ballot drop box here.](https://us.list-manage.com/gA2FK7OpETL?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8) And if you’ve already voted, make sure your friends and family vote, too!
Talk soon,
ps We lost Captain Picard this week. Pete is a huge Star Trek nerd, and when he guest-hosted _Jimmy Kimmel_ , he interviewed Sir Patrick Stewart, who surprised him with an original Star Trek script. [It's worth a watch.](https://us.list-manage.com/10VBSWrmY1E?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8) Godspeed, Captain.

Peter, You need to see this from NDRC President John Bisognano’s op-ed in Democracy Docket:
> [“Trump’s gerrymandering grab failed. But the war for democracy isn’t over”](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142562182/657312547/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_BizOped_email_20261030-NDRC-Tier1-BizOped_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20261030-NDRC-Tier1-BizOped_&utm_campaign=BizOped&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjY4ODM3MTQ3LWE2ZDQtZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMGQzYTU0NDQyZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=50W7lGmlasmBmaSsXTGnYS9Sz-OiEFZCUrijxJ01IuM=)
> —NDRC President John Bisognano, Democracy Docket
[The whole piece is worth a read](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142562183/657312548/1052264650?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_BizOped_email_20261030-NDRC-Tier1-BizOped_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20261030-NDRC-Tier1-BizOped_&utm_campaign=BizOped&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjY4ODM3MTQ3LWE2ZDQtZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMGQzYTU0NDQyZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=50W7lGmlasmBmaSsXTGnYS9Sz-OiEFZCUrijxJ01IuM=&emci=9bc0da9c-bdd3-f111-bf5b-00224824d4db&emdi=68837147-a6d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=8431045), but in case you’re pressed for time right now, we want to call your attention to two key points. Even though Republicans didn’t succeed in rigging enough maps to save their skins this year, they’re going to try again:
> “This victory, however, is a reprieve, not a resolution. If Republicans do lose the House, they’re all but certain to double down on their efforts to gerrymander heading into 2028 — to cheat and sidestep the voters rather than try to win them back.”
That's not speculation. That's based on our most up-to-date intel from the ground in several key states. As Biz puts it:
> “As soon as the polls close on Nov. 3, Republicans are anticipated to take up the pen again to try to enact new mid-decade gerrymanders. During the lame-duck period in states like Georgia and Texas, Republican-led state legislatures could attempt to rush through new, even more skewed maps, or change who controls map drawing, before a new governor is sworn in. Mississippi, South Carolina, Indiana and Kansas — where redraws were thwarted over the past year — are expected to begin their efforts anew to gerrymander without constraints.”
So we’ve got two critical missions right now: getting out the vote to help elect Democracy Defenders who are on the ballot for November 3rd —AND getting ready for the next wave of redraw showdowns that could kick off in a matter of days. clean_body: As soon as the polls close, we have very good reason to believe Republicans will race to draw new gerrymanders | Peter, You need to see this from NDRC President John Bisognano’s op-ed in Democracy Docket: = —NDRC President John Bisognano, Democracy Docket , but in case you’re pressed for time right now, we want to call your attention to two key points. Even though Republicans didn’t succeed in rigging enough maps to save their skins this year, they’re going to try again: “This victory, however, is a reprieve, not a resolution. If Republicans do lose the House, they’re all but certain to double down on their efforts to gerrymander heading into 2028 — to cheat and sidestep the voters rather than try to win them back.” That's not speculation. That's based on our most up-to-date intel from the ground in several key states. As Biz puts it: “As soon as the polls close on Nov. 3, Republicans are anticipated to take up the pen again to try to enact new mid-decade gerrymanders. During the lame-duck period in states like Georgia and Texas, Republican-led state legislatures could attempt to rush through new, even more skewed maps, or change who controls map drawing, before a new governor is sworn in. Mississippi, South Carolina, Indiana and Kansas — where redraws were thwarted over the past year — are expected to begin their efforts anew to gerrymander without constraints.” So we’ve got two critical missions right now: getting out the vote to help elect Democracy Defenders who are on the ballot for November 3rd —AND getting ready for the next wave of redraw showdowns that could kick off in a matter of days. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = Thank you, Team NDRC = = | | Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President. | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|--- National Democratic Redistricting Committee 712 H St NE, #25 Washington, DC 20002 United States if you'd like to receive fewer emails from the NDRC. name: Chris Pappas
subject: We’ve come so far.
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9891%2E582294%2EM_oTqY ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9891%2E582294%2EM_oTqY ]Chris Pappas for Senate

I wanted to
take a moment to reflect on how far we’ve come.

But if you don’t have time to read a longer message and want to show your
support, [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261030_3.sXPBwb&refcode=em20261030-3&t=1003&akid=9891%2E582294%2EM_oTqY ]please chip in $5 or any amount today.

I didn’t enter public service from a family of career politicians. My
roots are right here in Manchester, shaped behind the counter at my
family’s landmark restaurant.

Growing up working there taught me the value of hard work, accountability,
and serving our community. That’s the exact work ethic I wanted to bring
to Washington to fix a system that no longer works for everyday people.

Now in one of the most critical Senate races in the country, I’m ready to
keep being a voice for all Granite Staters.

We’ve come so far building a true grassroots movement across New
Hampshire, but the contrast in this race could not be clearer.

Our campaign is built by working people pitching in what they can when
they can, while John Sununu is backed by Donald Trump, MAGA billionaires,
and corporate PACs.

Sununu has sold out Granite Staters to corporate special interests like
Big Pharma and Wall Street and grew his net worth up to $35 million.
Granite Staters can’t trust him to fight for them as long as he can line
his own pockets.

With just 4 days left until Election Day, everything comes down to this
final stretch. I need your help to make sure we have the resources to
reach every last voter so we can protect this open seat and flip the
Senate blue in November.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261030_3.sXPBwb&refcode=em20261030-3&t=1004&akid=9891%2E582294%2EM_oTqY ]If you’re ready to help us cross the finish line, will you pitch in
$5 or whatever you can today?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261030_3.sXPBwb&amount=5&refcode=em20261030-3&t=1023&akid=9891%2E582294%2EM_oTqY ]Donate $5 »

Thank you,

Chris

**Boysko Bulletin Alert: Vote Saturday (10/31) or Tuesday, Election Day (11/3)**
---
Dear Peter,
---
Tomorrow is Halloween! I hope you and your family enjoy trick or treating!There are two days left for voting - for our federal representatives, for three amendments to the Virginia Constitution, a park bond initiative, and for my immediate neighbors, for the Herndon Town Council. Every vote matters. Constituents in the Senate District 38 are represented by Senator Mark Warner and either Representative James Walkinshaw or Representative Don Beyer. We are fortunate to be represented by people who share our values and work hard to ensure that all members of our community can live with dignity, making the most of their talents, with access to affordable housing, healthcare and education. They have all championed our federal workers when the federal Administration cut their jobs, impacting education, healthcare, employment, and other important government functions. Senator Warner, Congressman Beyer and Walkinshaw are true public servants and deserve our votes. Please make time to cast your ballots for them and for our ballot initiatives. Here’s a [video](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142562575/657313874/47729617?si=8Vuz7HUrzjvOqHui&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGM2ZDNiYWUtYTdkNC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=--CzgMAmzZU0HF_UIoLx9smJlSP6NYRPeB2X0B5HpMw=&emci=13fe300f-9bd4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=0c6d3bae-a7d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=22486556) about the Virginia Constitutional Amendments. Here’s a quick guide, vote yes if you agree that you should have:
* Freedom to decide for yourself about reproductive health with the advice and care from your doctor - not politicians
* Freedom to marry the person you love without government interference
* Freedom to vote and to be treated as a full-fledged citizen with the same rights and responsibilities as other Virginians after completing your incarceration when you return to the community

We expect a beautiful fall weekend - make the most of this time by voting and then relaxing, knowing that you’ve chosen candidates who work to support the most vulnerable members of our community and to allow all of us to live full lives with dignity, opportunity, safety and freedom. You are welcome to join me for the [Final Stretch Canvass](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142562576/657313875/719103261?utm_source=huntermilldems.beehiiv.com&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=less-than-two-weeks-more-doors-to-knock-more-polls-to-staff-let-s-go&_bhlid=16cd19cdab52b8b79f2d1faa306c54dba4423092&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGM2ZDNiYWUtYTdkNC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=--CzgMAmzZU0HF_UIoLx9smJlSP6NYRPeB2X0B5HpMw=&emci=13fe300f-9bd4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=0c6d3bae-a7d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=22486556) with Supervisor Alcorn and Delegate Keys-Gamarra. Let’s get out the vote together!

Jennifer B. **What’s Your Voting Plan?** **Check Your Registration, Voter Location, Early Voting Hours ** You can find the election information you need at the [state election website](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142562579/657313878/1040056213?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGM2ZDNiYWUtYTdkNC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=--CzgMAmzZU0HF_UIoLx9smJlSP6NYRPeB2X0B5HpMw=&emci=13fe300f-9bd4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=0c6d3bae-a7d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=22486556) or the [Fairfax County election website](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142562580/657313879/-150005810?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGM2ZDNiYWUtYTdkNC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=--CzgMAmzZU0HF_UIoLx9smJlSP6NYRPeB2X0B5HpMw=&emci=13fe300f-9bd4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=0c6d3bae-a7d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=22486556). You can vote Saturday, 10/31, at [early voting sites](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142562581/657313880/112561586?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGM2ZDNiYWUtYTdkNC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=--CzgMAmzZU0HF_UIoLx9smJlSP6NYRPeB2X0B5HpMw=&emci=13fe300f-9bd4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=0c6d3bae-a7d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=22486556) and on Tuesday, election day, 11/3, at [your assigned voting precinct](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142562582/657313881/-804946760?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGM2ZDNiYWUtYTdkNC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=--CzgMAmzZU0HF_UIoLx9smJlSP6NYRPeB2X0B5HpMw=&emci=13fe300f-9bd4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=0c6d3bae-a7d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=22486556). **Three Amendments to the Virginia Constitution on the 11/3 Ballot** **Reproductive Freedom Amendment** The Reproductive Freedom Amendment protects access to the full range of reproductive health care and puts the power where it belongs—with Virginians, their families, and their doctors. No matter your faith or personal beliefs, these are decisions that should be made personally, not by the government. The amendment was crafted to follow the current laws in Virginia, to take the politics out of reproductive healthcare, and to protect the fundamental freedom to make these decisions for ourselves. The time has come to let the voters have the final say. You are probably aware that the US Supreme Court Dobbs decision removed the fundamental right to privacy regarding abortion, leaving it up to the states. The Constitutional Amendment will guarantee Virginians the freedom to make and carry out decisions relating to one's own prenatal care, childbirth, postpartum care, contraception, abortion care, miscarriage management, and fertility care. I am working with the [Virginians for Reproductive Freedom](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142562583/657313882/-494596654?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGM2ZDNiYWUtYTdkNC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=--CzgMAmzZU0HF_UIoLx9smJlSP6NYRPeB2X0B5HpMw=&emci=13fe300f-9bd4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=0c6d3bae-a7d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=22486556) to encourage people to vote for the amendment. Now is the time to act—to secure reproductive freedom for generations to come. **I urge you to vote yes.** **Marriage Amendment** Question 2 would repeal Virginia's now archaic 2006 Marshall-Newman Amendment, a ban on marriage between same-sex couples that remains in our Virginia Constitution today, and replace it with an affirmative guarantee that the government must treat all marriages equally under the law. It would enshrine the freedom for adult couples to marry, as the current law in Virginia allows. [Virginians for Marriage Equality](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142562584/657313883/-2015354088?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGM2ZDNiYWUtYTdkNC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=--CzgMAmzZU0HF_UIoLx9smJlSP6NYRPeB2X0B5HpMw=&emci=13fe300f-9bd4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=0c6d3bae-a7d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=22486556) is a coalition of Virginia families, couples, faith leaders, and advocacy organizations working to protect the freedom to marry in Virginia. This amendment ensures the freedom to marry the person you love is a right enjoyed by every Virginian for generations to come. **I urge you to vote yes.** **Restoration of Rights Amendment** The third Constitutional Amendment that you will see on your ballot pertains to the restoration of rights for returning citizens after completion of their incarceration. Virginia is an outlier in its current policy and is a vestige of the 1902 Jim Crow Constitution. Most other states have automatic restoration of rights. The Constitutional Amendment creates an explicit constitutional right to vote for every eligible Virginian. It would protect against current and future attacks on voting rights by taking the right to vote out of politicians’ hands. The amendment also protects people with disabilities from automatically losing their right to vote when put under a guardianship by empowering judges to decide case-by-case if that person understands the act of voting. I urge you to vote yes. Learn more at [https://www.varighttovote.org/about-us](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142562585/657313884/-146069721?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGM2ZDNiYWUtYTdkNC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=--CzgMAmzZU0HF_UIoLx9smJlSP6NYRPeB2X0B5HpMw=&emci=13fe300f-9bd4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=0c6d3bae-a7d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=22486556). **Herndon Town Council Election Update** The mayor and all members of the Herndon Town Council are on the ballot this November. If you are a town resident, living in Herndon 1, 2 or 3 precincts, you can vote in the town election. **Give Back**

clean_body: | | | | Boysko Bulletin Alert: Vote Saturday (10/31) or Tuesday, Election Day (11/3) Dear Peter, Tomorrow is Halloween! I hope you and your family enjoy trick or treating!There are two days left for voting - for our federal representatives, for three amendments to the Virginia Constitution, a park bond initiative, and for my immediate neighbors, for the Herndon Town Council. Every vote matters. Constituents in the Senate District 38 are represented by Senator Mark Warner and either Representative James Walkinshaw or Representative Don Beyer. We are fortunate to be represented by people who share our values and work hard to ensure that all members of our community can live with dignity, making the most of their talents, with access to affordable housing, healthcare and education. They have all championed our federal workers when the federal Administration cut their jobs, impacting education, healthcare, employment, and other important government functions. Senator Warner, Congressman Beyer and Walkinshaw are true public servants and deserve our votes. Please make time to cast your ballots for them and for our ballot initiatives. Here’s a about the Virginia Constitutional Amendments. Here’s a quick guide, vote yes if you agree that you should have: Freedom to decide for yourself about reproductive health with the advice and care from your doctor - not politicians Freedom to marry the person you love without government interference Freedom to vote and to be treated as a full-fledged citizen with the same rights and responsibilities as other Virginians after completing your incarceration when you return to the community We expect a beautiful fall weekend - make the most of this time by voting and then relaxing, knowing that you’ve chosen candidates who work to support the most vulnerable members of our community and to allow all of us to live full lives with dignity, opportunity, safety and freedom. You are welcome to join me for the with Supervisor Alcorn and Delegate Keys-Gamarra. Let’s get out the vote together! Kindest regards, Jennifer B. BoyskoMember, Senate of Virginia Representing the newly created 38th Senate District making up the northernmost portions of Fairfax County (Great Falls, Herndon, McLean, Reston, WolfTrap, parts of unincorporated Vienna and a slice of Falls Church) PS If you would like to support my work, please visit =. What’s Your Voting Plan? Check Your Registration, Voter Location, Early Voting Hours You can find the election information you need at the or the . You can vote Saturday, 10/31, at and on Tuesday, election day, 11/3, at . Three Amendments to the Virginia Constitution on the 11/3 Ballot Reproductive Freedom Amendment The Reproductive Freedom Amendment protects access to the full range of reproductive health care and puts the power where it belongs—with Virginians, their families, and their doctors. No matter your faith or personal beliefs, these are decisions that should be made personally, not by the government. The amendment was crafted to follow the current laws in Virginia, to take the politics out of reproductive healthcare, and to protect the fundamental freedom to make these decisions for ourselves. The time has come to let the voters have the final say. You are probably aware that the US Supreme Court Dobbs decision removed the fundamental right to privacy regarding abortion, leaving it up to the states. The Constitutional Amendment will guarantee Virginians the freedom to make and carry out decisions relating to one's own prenatal care, childbirth, postpartum care, contraception, abortion care, miscarriage management, and fertility care. I am working with the to encourage people to vote for the amendment. Now is the time to act—to secure reproductive freedom for generations to come. I urge you to vote yes. Marriage Amendment Question 2 would repeal Virginia's now archaic 2006 Marshall-Newman Amendment, a ban on marriage between same-sex couples that remains in our Virginia Constitution today, and replace it with an affirmative guarantee that the government must treat all marriages equally under the law. It would enshrine the freedom for adult couples to marry, as the current law in Virginia allows. is a coalition of Virginia families, couples, faith leaders, and advocacy organizations working to protect the freedom to marry in Virginia. This amendment ensures the freedom to marry the person you love is a right enjoyed by every Virginian for generations to come. I urge you to vote yes. Restoration of Rights Amendment The third Constitutional Amendment that you will see on your ballot pertains to the restoration of rights for returning citizens after completion of their incarceration. Virginia is an outlier in its current policy and is a vestige of the 1902 Jim Crow Constitution. Most other states have automatic restoration of rights. The Constitutional Amendment creates an explicit constitutional right to vote for every eligible Virginian. It would protect against current and future attacks on voting rights by taking the right to vote out of politicians’ hands. The amendment also protects people with disabilities from automatically losing their right to vote when put under a guardianship by empowering judges to decide case-by-case if that person understands the act of voting. I urge you to vote yes. Learn more at . Herndon Town Council Election Update The mayor and all members of the Herndon Town Council are on the ballot this November. If you are a town resident, living in Herndon 1, 2 or 3 precincts, you can vote in the town election. body:
Here's why I'm writing to you specifically:
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, I know you hear from my team often, so I wanted to write to you myself today because we've hit a moment in this race that I don't think anyone saw coming a year ago.
**A new poll this week shows me leading Greg Abbott, 49% to 46%. It’s the seventh public poll this fall to show me ahead.**
Abbott had never been shown trailing in a public poll before last month — in any race he’s ever run. In twelve years and three campaigns for governor, Abbott has never faced anything like this.
And we’ve gotten here while being outspent 5 to 1. Abbott has spent $181 million in this race. We’ve spent $35 million, the same amount he spent in the last month alone.
But here's what worries me: **Tomorrow night is our final end-of-month fundraising deadline before the election.**
_**This is the moment when your support in this race matters most, Peter.**_
**That’s why we set a goal to raise $3 million this week, before the October 31st deadline, which would bring us to $10 million raised in October. This is the minimum amount of money we need to raise, and falling short is not an option. As of writing this email, we’re 93% of the way there.**
According to our records, you haven’t made your first contribution to this campaign yet, and I wanted to make sure you heard about where we stand from me before the deadline passes.
If you’ve been waiting to see whether this race is really winnable, this is your answer. This race is a real toss-up, and in four days it will be decided. The window where your grassroots donation can still reach voters is right now.
[**Will you make your first-ever contribution right now, even just $5, and help us raise the $3,000,000 we urgently need by tomorrow at midnight?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261030_3_message.kks93q&refcode=em20261030-2603&amount=5&t=3&akid=2603%2E299639%2EF-zPEM)

Gina

Check in with your friends, family, neighbors, and community members to encourage them to vote. Saturday voting is available this weekend in all 92 counties, and Marion County, St Joseph County, and select other counties have locations open on Sunday -- it’s that easy! Visit [indiana.votinginfotool.org](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142563797/657317541/1201557060?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZDBiNzhmNC1hYmQ0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=e7LLnDDyMwnWL14cE8_UYJQck6LhE_g3Jbwzu5-hBG4=&emci=c8abe388-a0d4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=cd0b78f4-abd4-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=4925535) to plan your voting and find your polling place hours. **Still have an absentee ballot?** It is recommended that you avoid mailing it and bring it to an early voting location or to your county courthouse. On Election Day, you must either take it directly to your county courthouse, or surrender it at your polling location and cast a regular ballot. Mail-in ballots must be RECEIVED by 6 PM local time on Election Day in order to be counted. Make sure you date your ballot envelope with the date you signed it. ‬A missing date will result in your absentee ballot being rejected. ****

Hoosiers are worried about the cost of childcare and rising utility bills, while Republicans are only focused on protecting their own political power. # [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41626%2E3422442%2EySwPcQ)
Peter,
All our hard work over the past year comes down to what happens before Tuesday.
Truth to Power is backing a slate of candidates that will go to Congress to fight for working families without taking a cent in corporate PAC money. _We only have 4 days to make sure they get over the finish line._
These are candidates like Abdul El-Sayed and Peggy Flanagan, Cait Conley and Mai Vang. I’ve run in close races like theirs before, and I know late support can make all the difference between winning and losing.
**[That’s why we set a goal to raise another $3,000 before our end-of-month fundraising deadline tomorrow. Can you give $5 right now to help us reach our goal and elect these leaders?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20261030_1_ak.jyI239&refcode=em20261030-41626&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41626%2E3422442%2EySwPcQ)**
The candidates on our slate cannot win alone. Their opponents have outside groups and corporate PACs coming in to tip the scales in the GOP’s favor—Truth to Power is part of the team making sure they can fight on even footing.
With less than a week to go, support from this grassroots movement will allow them to make extra investments that will get them the votes they need to win.
**[I’m counting on you to help us reach this goal, Peter. Chip in $5 or whatever you can afford to help us raise our final $3,000 before October ends and send our slate of candidates to Congress.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20261030_1_ak.jyI239&refcode=em20261030-41626&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41626%2E3422442%2EySwPcQ)**

Thank you,
Katie Porter

Former U.S. Congresswoman Katie Porter founded Truth to Power to support the campaigns of her fellow Democrats. name: Kristen McDonald Rivet
subject: Michigan is one of the most crucial battlegrounds in the country
body:
|
#
Friend, I’ll be honest: Michigan is one of the most crucial battlegrounds in the country – and what happens here next Tuesday could decide who controls Congress. We know it. So do national Republicans. Right now, they’re zeroing in on my race – and they’re just as determined to hold onto MI-04 and MI-10, two Republican-held seats that **Sean McCann** and **Christina Hines** are working to flip blue. Friend, I’ve worked hard to deliver for mid-Michigan: expanding access to health care, fighting corruption, and lowering everyday costs for working families. Christina and Sean share that same commitment to real solutions, and together, I know we can get even more done. But right now, our races are proving to be some of the toughest in the country. That’s why MAGA Republicans are doing (and spending!) whatever it takes to win. We need the resources to fight back, because winning across Michigan will get us _even_ closer to taking back the House. That’s where you come in. [**If you can, will you chip in $10, $20, or even $35 to our Michigan Battleground Victory Fund? It's Halloween weekend — the season for haunted houses and scary costumes.
But the truly frightening thought this year isn't a ghost or a goblin. It's two years of Carmela Conroy and a Democrat majority in Congress: higher taxes, open borders, and Eastern Washington's voice shut out completely.
That's a scare no one here can afford.
Here's the good news: you can stop it right now, and it takes two minutes.
**If your ballot is still sitting on your counter, this is the weekend to return it.**
In Washington, this race won't be decided on Tuesday; it's being decided right now, one returned ballot at a time. Fill yours out, drop it in a ballot drop box or in the mail this weekend, and then check with a friend, a neighbor, or a family member and make sure theirs is in too.

name: Dan Ahlers
subject: Our closing message to South Dakota
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ahlers for Governor
body:
This ad is the last one voters will see, help us make it count

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/6fb64dd976c7/health-care-you-deserve-10598465?e=cee7b49c04)

---
| |

Friends,
It’s almost time. After over 50,000 miles on the road across our great state, thousands of inspiring conversations with South Dakotans, and visiting with anyone I could find from Britton to Hermosa, I’ve learned one big thing from South Dakotans. The status quo, 50 years of one party rule from the governor’s mansion, can’t stand. That’s why our closing message strikes right into the core of the problem facing our state. Our leaders don’t want to change. I wanted to share that message with you.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/IRRD20pGfbK?e=cee7b49c04&c2id=3adc23449cf80dcda430cceaf3c4b05d)
| | Our final message is the most important because it is what voters will take with them as they head to the polls this Tuesday. We need your help to get it out there.
_**South Dakota is ready for change. We want you to be a part of it.**_
Larry Rhoden is the byproduct of complacency: 50 years of standing idly by while our schools deteriorate, our farmers pack up shop, and our roads crumble.
We’ve worked our way up, all in the interest of South Dakota, trying to talk to every teacher and farmer in between. We know what it’s like to be the underdog, Larry Rhoden doesn’t.
This race is within striking distance, and I need your help to push us over.
---

| | Folks, there's a lot of talk these days about whether members of Congress have a spine. It's a fair question. But I'd point out that a spine, all by itself, doesn't move anything. What moves a load is **muscle.** Right now, Congress doesn’t have much of it. **In four days, we can change that.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142565885/657323854/-373287771?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_261030_FR_Muscle_A0_na_U1_X3_M4&amount=20&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhMTg2OGIwYS1iMGQ0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=aZB8pgVRtaJN5PC5kt_1cR7-US_wl92Qr49nzEPR-9w=) I joined the Navy at 17, just before women were finally allowed to serve on combatant ships. I was one of the first women to spend my career on these ships. I was also one of the first women to graduate from the Navy's Nuclear Power School. Six deployments. 20 years at sea. Eight nuclear reactors and 700 nuclear operators under my command. Then, two victories in a battleground House district no one thought I could win. In my first term, I was ranked one of the most effective freshman members of Congress. I secured $455 million to restore the Chesapeake Bay after decades of neglect and broken promises
I served on the January 6th Committee, knowing full well it could cost me my seat
I fought for our veterans, for affordable health care, and for the Hampton Roads economy that supports both Jen Kiggans has held this seat for four years. She hasn’t moved mountains. She hasn’t lifted the burden on Hampton Roads families. She hasn’t even lifted a finger. That’s the choice on Tuesday: a leader with backbone and muscle versus a spineless MAGA puppet. Right now, **Kiggans and her party bosses have already spent more than $8M to beat me. Peter, From Bucks County to Philadelphia, our members and volunteers are having conversations with their neighbors about the future our communities deserve. We’re knocking on doors, making calls, and reaching voters online because we know that when working people organize together, we can build the power to change who represents us. **This Election Day, we have an opportunity to help flip Congress blue and make it more progressive. OnePA is proud to support Bob Harvie in Pennsylvania’s 1st Congressional District and Chris Rabb in the 3rd.** In Bucks County, Bob is challenging Republican Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick in a county Kamala Harris won. It’s a major opportunity to pick up a congressional seat and replace a politician who voted for devastating health care cuts to fund tax breaks for the wealthy with a leader who will fight to lower costs for working families. In Philadelphia, Chris is building a strong multiracial coalition and energizing young voters. This summer, he became the first in a wave of progressive candidates to defeat establishment Democrats, and now we’re organizing to send this longtime champion for workers, immigrants, and racial and economic justice to Congress. **We know that statements alone don’t win elections. It takes people showing up for their communities, talking with neighbors about the issues that affect our lives, and making sure voters have the information and resources they need to cast their ballots.**
That’s why we’re running a massive GOTV campaign across Pennsylvania. Our organizers and volunteers are knocking on doors, phone banking, and text banking to reach voters and help turn community support into votes.
We’re also working with content creators who can speak to their communities online about the candidates, the issues, and how to vote. These trusted local voices help us reach more people and bring new voters into the movement we’re building together.
Every conversation is part of building a Pennsylvania where working people have a stronger voice in the decisions that shape our lives.**By organizing together now, we can help elect leaders who will stand up to corporate power, fight for the resources our communities need, and keep building the collective power to hold them accountable.**

clean_body: From Bucks County to Philadelphia, our communities are coming together to elect leaders who will stand with working families. | | Peter, From Bucks County to Philadelphia, our members and volunteers are having conversations with their neighbors about the future our communities deserve. We’re knocking on doors, making calls, and reaching voters online because we know that when working people organize together, we can build the power to change who represents us. This Election Day, we have an opportunity to help flip Congress blue and make it more progressive. OnePA is proud to support Bob Harvie in Pennsylvania’s 1st Congressional District and Chris Rabb in the 3rd. In Bucks County, Bob is challenging Republican Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick in a county Kamala Harris won. It’s a major opportunity to pick up a congressional seat and replace a politician who voted for devastating health care cuts to fund tax breaks for the wealthy with a leader who will fight to lower costs for working families. In Philadelphia, Chris is building a strong multiracial coalition and energizing young voters. This summer, he became the first in a wave of progressive candidates to defeat establishment Democrats, and now we’re organizing to send this longtime champion for workers, immigrants, and racial and economic justice to Congress. | | We know that statements alone don’t win elections. It takes people showing up for their communities, talking with neighbors about the issues that affect our lives, and making sure voters have the information and resources they need to cast their ballots. That’s why we’re running a massive GOTV campaign across Pennsylvania. Our organizers and volunteers are knocking on doors, phone banking, and text banking to reach voters and help turn community support into votes. We’re also working with content creators who can speak to their communities online about the candidates, the issues, and how to vote. These trusted local voices help us reach more people and bring new voters into the movement we’re building together. Every conversation is part of building a Pennsylvania where working people have a stronger voice in the decisions that shape our lives.By organizing together now, we can help elect leaders who will stand up to corporate power, fight for the resources our communities need, and keep building the collective power to hold them accountable.
